News.title: ‘Trash’ Russian reality star, 22, learns fate after arrest for parading naked through Moscow amid Putin’s porn crackdown
News.content:
A TRASH blogging reality star has discovered her fate after she was arrested for strutting through the streets of Moscow completely naked.

Anastasia Bragina, 22, has narrowly avoided a lengthy prison sentence in a Russian jail amid Vladimir Putin‘s sweeping crackdown on the porn industry.



The controversial star – known for her bold and racey content – was handed a three year suspended sentence at a Moscow court today.

Bragina found herself in hot water with the Kremlin after she walked the streets of Moscow completely nude in a live stream to a 21 million-strong audience.



Defending the stunt, she said she wanted to “break free from all limitations.”

Bragina – a former contestant on popular TV reality show Dom-2 – was the fifth Russian influencer to face pornography charges in the crackdown on OnlyFans and other “Western platforms” seen as promoting online sex.

Following her incarceration dodge, a seemingly reformed Bragina told reporters: “I used to take things so lightly, but now I’ve become grounded and realise that every misstep carries responsibility,

“I will dedicate these next three years to meeting a man and building a family….



“I want to be a mum.”

Ekaterina Mizulina, high-profile head of Russia’s Safe Internet League and a member of Putin’s Civic Chamber, initially reported Anastasia to the Interior Ministry and Investigative Committee.

She accused Bragina of “dissemination of pornography among children” and said she had “completely lost her mind” following her Moscow stunt.



Mizulina continued: “The trash-blogger is publicly corrupting children on her platforms, constantly appearing naked in video circles, holding conversations in that state with children mainly on intimate subjects, and also giving schoolchildren various pieces of depraved advice.”

Mizulina – who was rumoured to have had a romantic relationship with Putin – is spearheading the crackdown on “anti-traditional values”.

She advocates tight censorship on the Internet, fines and other sanctions against the media and social networks.

Her philosopher father Professor Mikhail Mizulin, 71, is a leading academic in Moscow, and her mother Yelena is a pro-Putin senator in the Russian parliament.

In July, fellow OnlyFans star Sofya Vershinina, 21, has been convicted of producing and distributing explicit online videos in a Moscow court.



She was ordered to pay £45,000 and was barred from appearing online, using the internet or from running digital business for three years in a massive blow to her income.

Russian prosecutors say she earned £300,000 from selling X-rated videos and sold intimate content on Telegram messenger while living in an elite Moscow skyscraper penthouse.

Another model and influencer Diana Shurygina, 27, is currently custody awaiting trial.

Sources say the case against her centres on “intimate content” she allegedly sold to paying subscribers on OnlyFans.

Anastasia Ovsyannikova, 24, known under the stage name Nastya Kholod, was also held on suspicion of illegal production and circulation of pornographic materials.



She and Diana made adult content for OnlyFans together and separately.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As Putin continued to take on the Russian porn industry, legal experts warn the net could widen even further to enforce so-called “traditional values”.

Trash blogging is a form of online content creation where creators broadcast degrading, humiliating or dangerous acts live on the internet for money.

News.title: Military aircraft entering ‘spurious’ flight data sparked airport chaos which saw planes grounded & passengers stranded
News.content:
A MILITARY aircraft entering “spurious” flight data sparked the air traffic control meltdown which grounded thousands of planes.

The UK military aircraft submitted a flight plan it is understood, which caused several hours of chaos for the National Air Traffic Services (Nats) on Tuesday.

British skies were shutdown for four hours and it took several attempts for the systems, which manage 8,000 flights a day, to restart.

Kathryn Leahy, Nats operations director, told industry bosses about the source of the disorder during a briefing on Tuesday evening, an insider said.





This comes after Nats promised airline bosses that a rogue flight plan would not derail the system after a similar disaster in 2023 which saw thousands of flights grounded.

Speaking to the FT, one airline executive, said: “We were told the [recommendations after 2023] had been fully implemented, but to tell you the truth, we never saw the evidence.”

News.title: Paedophile, 62, who raped and assaulted multiple children keeping one as ‘sexual slave’ jailed for 37 years
News.content:
CAMPAIGN OF ABUSE Paedophile, 62, who raped and assaulted multiple children keeping one as ‘sexual slave’ jailed for 37 years

A VILE paedophile who raped and assaulted multiple children, keeping one as a “sexual slave” has now begun a 37-year prison sentence.

Paul Benstock, 62, was found guilty following his trial in July at Leeds Crown Court of more than 40 sickening offences dating back over decades.

These included rape, sexual assault and physical assaults.



During his trial, the jury heard that Benstock used fear, violence, intimidation and humiliation to keep his victims silent.



Judge Neil Clark said he had committed the “most unpleasant sexual offending that can be imagined” and treated one victim as his “sexual slave”.

He said: “You ruined their lives by using and threatening extreme violence.”

Benstock, of East Ardsley, West Yorkshire, showed no emotion as he was hit with an extended 37-year jail sentence with the judge finding him to be a dangerous offender.



Prosecutor Kitty Colley read out heartbreaking statements written by his victims to the court.

One victim said he still “wakes up fighting” Benstock and hasn’t gotten over his ordeal.

He added that he had turned to drugs and alcohol in order to “numb the pain”.

A female victim said: “You not only stole my childhood, you stole my adult life too.



“I have nightmares so often it’s just better and easier to stay awake.

“I have completely lost myself.

“You are a monster who used power and control to take what you wanted.

“I carry so much shame around every day. It’s not mine, it’s yours.

“I will never forgive you for putting me through the court process.



“You have never taken any accountability.”

Benstock’s abuse dated back to the 1990s, the court was told.

It was only after his last victim came forward and spoke out that others then followed.

His youngest victim was aged just nine and he would then threaten them into staying silent.

As well as sexually abusing youngsters, he would also attack them with weapons in ways Judge Clark said were “ghastly”.



After his arrest, it was discovered he has been searching out child abuse images online just the day before.

He was given a 30-year custodial sentence, with a seven-year extended licence period.

Benstock was put on the sex offenders registry for life.

Detective Sergeant Michelle Barnes, of Leeds Safeguarding Unit, said previously: “We had one victim come forward to us to reporting that they had been the victim of offences at the hands of Benstock.

“As a result of our enquiries, we identified four other victims who then also had the courage to detail the crimes they had been subjected to.



“Much of Benstock’s offending was against victims who were children at the time.

“His victims have shown incredible bravery in giving us detailed accounts of what has taken place and then again supporting the trial process by giving evidence when Benstock refused to take accountability for his awful crimes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Benstock is yet to be sentenced and I know that that date will be another significant milestone in the journey that his victims have been through, but I do hope that today having got these verdicts that it brings them some comfort knowing that they were believed.

“I do not underestimate how hard it is to take that step to report physical or sexual offences to the police but if you have been a victim, please reach out for help and support when you are ready.”

News.title: Politicians and celebrities should never be able to decide what counts as news, Sun Editor says in major speech
News.content:
WE NEED FREE PRESS Politicians and celebrities should never be able to decide what counts as news, Sun Editor says in major speech

Credit: Francesco Guidicini

POLITICIANS, celebrities or the State should never be able to decide what counts as news, the Editor-in-Chief of The Sun has said.

Victoria Newton defended the role of the popular Press to deliver stories with “purpose, reach and a bit of mischief” during a key speech on media freedom.

Faced with the challenges of disinformation and AI, she said she is “optimistic” about the lasting power of proper journalism.

Ms Newton said: “There are still powerful people who would like the press to be more tightly controlled.



“They usually say this is about standards, or privacy, or responsibility, and sometimes it is.

“But sometimes it is really about those who have lived by publicity, deciding they don’t like scrutiny when the story turns against them.

“Of course, there must be rules and standards. But the answer can never be a system where politicians, celebrities or the state decide what counts as news.”

Ms Newton said The Sun’s exclusive stories on disgraced BBC news reader Huw Edwards showed the importance of an independent tabloid press.

When this paper exposed Edwards for paying a vulnerable teenager for intimate images, it faced a “firestorm of abuse”, she said.

She said: “Only the popular press could have exposed this paedophile.

“And, while saddened, I am proud that we were brave enough to publish it.”

She added that journalism produced by reporters at The Sun is key to “beating AI slop”, and technology companies should be prepared to pay for it if they want to benefit from it.

The Hugh Cudlipp Lecture, delivered in London on Thursday, was created in memory of the former editorial director of the Daily Mirror and is an annual platform for senior media leaders to share views on the industry.

News.title: Mum, 21, and son, 5, killed alongside boyfriend as landslide buries their home as they slept during horror storm
News.content:
FAMILY TRAGEDY Mum, 21, and son, 5, killed alongside boyfriend as landslide buries their home as they slept during horror storm

A YOUNG boy, his mum and her boyfriend have been killed after a devastating landslide decimated their home while they slept.

Vinicius Lima, 5, Jaqueline Lima, 21, and her partner Kauan da Silva, 21, were found buried deep under mounds of mud and debris after a horror storm struck southern Brazil.



An urgent search operation was launched for missing locals when the extreme weather hit Parana state on Thursday morning.

The family were sleeping in the same bed at the time of the tragedy.



A fleet of emergency services – including 10 firefighters – were dispatched to the scene at the Ronda neighbourhood of Ponta Grossa.

Firefighters said the landslide struck the house at around 8.44am, bringing down a wall and part of the roof.



To avoid another collapse, emergency crews stabilized the building before they were able to enter the property.

Sadly, all three victims were pronounced dead at the scene despite attempts to revive them.



The disaster came as severe storms hit Paraná, causing flooding and flash floods across several municipalities.

Weather authorities also confirmed two tornadoes in the state within around 24 hours, one near Francisco Alves and another in the community of Boa Vista, in Espigao Alto do Iguacu.

More than 22,000 properties were also left without electricity at the height of the storms, according to power company Copel.

The tragedy unfolded as the country prepares for the brunt of El Niño, with forecasts warning of torrential rains and severe flooding in the months ahead.

Heavy rain poses huge risks to Brazil’s built-up cities, where urban surfaces prevent water from draining away.



Earlier this year at least 59 people were killed in catastrophic flooding in Brazil’s Minas Gerais state.

Homes were swallowed by raging waters and more than 230 people had to be rescued from the swell.

It follows a pattern of extreme weather events driven by El Niño, which has caused widespread devastation across large parts of Asia.

Last month, thousands of people died in flash flood in Nepal when a torrent of flood water, mud and debris swept along the Tibetan border.

The disaster occurred when a glacier collapsed on August 26 after which At least 1,380 bodies have so far been pulled from the wreckage.



The Nepalese government ordered DNA samples to be taken from all the bodies which have not been identified or claimed by loved ones.

News.title: Shocking moment top Buddhist monk is caught having sex with secret lover as pair arrested over £2m embezzlement plot
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a top Buddhist monk is caught having sex with his secret lover before being arrested over a £2m embezzlement plot.

Scandalous footage of Phra Wachirayan Wi, 66, smooching a woman identified as Punyavee Rungrueang, 47, in his home was widely broadcast on Thai media.



In Thailand, Buddhist monks take a vow of celibacy and also renounce material possessions.

The CCTV clip of the pair starts with them kissing on the same chair before in graphic video they begin having sex on top of the dining table.



The footage was discovered by police during an investigation into the monk on suspicion of embezzlement.

He was arrested on Thursday on suspicion of stealing millions of pounds worth of funds, alongside the woman he was caught having sex with.

The woman is accused of helping her lover convert and conceal the cash in an elaborate scheme.

Cops launched an investigation into Phra Wachirayan, an abbot at the Wat Phutthaisawan temple in Ayutthaya, in mid-July after receiving a tip off accusing him of misconduct.



Two streams of money linked to donation receipts issued in the temple’s name were identified.

“But the money from both streams did not enter the temple’s account”, lead police investigator Pattanasak Bupphasuwan said.

“Not a single baht,” he added.



A raid on Phra Wachirayan’s home uncovered cash and gold bars worth 100million baht (£2.2million).

The abbot was defrocked shortly after his arrest. He has yet to comment.

Thailand‘s Buddhist institution has been plagued with reports of monks breaking their vow of celibacy, trafficking drugs and committing financial crimes.

The latest arrests come just over a year after another sex-and-blackmail case involving senior monks rocked Thailand’s monastic community.

In July last year, police opened a hotline for people to report “misbehaving monks”.



The service was launched after at least nine monks were exposed for having sex with a woman identified as Wilawan Emsawat, 36.

Wilawan then blackmailed them with photos and videos of the acts to extort a whopping nine million pounds.

The scandal was exposed when a Phra Thep Wachirapamok, a widely respected monk from his Buddhist temple in central Bangkok, abruptly renounced his monkhood and vanished.

But it soon emerged that Wachirapamok, better known as Arch, was allegedly in an illicit relationship with Emsawat, who reportedly claimed to be pregnant.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A sweep of the woman’s house found five mobile phones with tens of thousands of files reportedly containing compromising footage of the missing monk.



Police Major General Charoonkiat Pankaew, deputy commissioner of the Cybercrime Investigation Bureau, said more than 12 Buddhist temples were under scrutiny following the scandal.

News.title: Horrifying moment leopard breaks out of cage and savages worker as colleague desperately tries to bat beast
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a sick leopard savagely attacked a forest guard after breaking out of its cage.

The ailing animal suddenly burst open the cage door and lunged at 57-year-old Buddhijung Gurung in the Lamjung District in central Nepal.



Footage shows the worker scrambling with the leopard as it continued to maul him while a colleague attempted to hit it with a rod on September 10.

Bystanders could be heard shouting as the enraged beast finally breaks away from him.



As people fled the area, the leopard knocked over a motorcycle which momentarily pinned the animal down.

Buddhijing suffered injuries to his left hand and face and was rushed to the Provincial Hospital in Besisahar for treatment, according to cops.



The footage before the attack shows a leopard locked in a small cage on top of a small truck after it was rescued near the Dhung Khola area.



It had been tranquilised after they found it in a sickly condition near Dhung Khola in the Besisahar Municpality, earlier in that afternoon.

It was scheduled to be transferred to a wildlife rescue centre for treatment.

Two men are seen lifting the cage from the vehicle before they moved it to another larger enclosure.

Later, the predator is seen roaming around the forest office and climbing up a pillar.

The staff used cages and barriers in order to contain it before causing any more harm.



The presence of the animal sparked fear among local residents in the nearby Besisahar market area.

The police were deployed around the forest office and ordered staff to stay inside when the leopard went on a rampage.

News.title: Brit, 35, yelled ‘I’m a gangster’ before ‘launching brutal knife attack at Bali hotel leaving worker blind in one eye’
News.content:
A BRIT traveller who allegedly left a hotel employee blind in one eye yelled “I’m a gangster” before launching the brutal knife attack.

Aaron Michel, 35, is facing 12 years in prison for allegedly stabbing the receptionist during a drunken rampage on Menjangan Island in May.



The suspect was turned down when he demanded staff to book him a room at the Indonesian hotel, a court heard this week.

He is said to have yelled at receptionist Ida Santika before the alleged attack: “I’m a gangster, and I want to party.”



Shocking CCTV footage showed him lashing out at the hotel worker who was left blind in one eye and with serious hand injuries.

Michel, from London, was arrested shortly after in a nearby town as he attempted to flee the island.

He appeared in Singaraja regional court this week charged with possessing a sharp weapon and assault causing serious injury.

Prosecutor Kadek Adi Pramarta requested that the judge jail him for 12 years.



He said: “The defendant’s actions caused the victim to suffer permanent blindness in his left eye, and he cannot move two of his fingers.”

Michel was behaving aggressively when he arrived at the hotel on the night of May 5 this year, the court heard.

Santika said: “I received a phone call from a security guard who said there was a guest who was going to view a room.



“The security guard said the guest was under the influence of alcohol.”

He added: “I went to meet him in the car park. I saw the defendant carrying three bottles of alcohol.

“I then asked, ‘Can I help you?’ He replied, ‘I’m a gangster, and I want to party.’

“He was so drunk that I refused to allow him access to view the room.”

Santika said he was then attacked “within seconds”.



The alleged victim said: “I then felt blood coming from my left eye and left hand. The defendant then got into his car and fled.

“I have not yet been able to forgive him.”

The case has been adjourned until next week.

With more than six million international visitors annually, Bali has become a popular destination for Brits.

But the influx of millions of “cashed- up” holidaymakers has transformed the once tranquil holiday destination into a crime hotspot.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The island has rapidly emerged as a honeypot for international drug traffickers and street violence and robbery is on the rise.

News.title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying
News.content:
MPs have voted against proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end.

Following a debate in which both sides made emotional speeches, the House of Commons voted 286 to 270, majority 16, against the proposed legislation.

The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill would have allowed adults with fewer than six months to live to apply to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

A similar bill in the last parliamentary session was supported by MPs before stalling in the House of Lords. The decision from MPs on Friday rules out the prospect of changes to the law on assisted dying in the short-term.

The bill tabled by Labour MP Lauren Edwards will make no further progress, although MPs and peers could make another attempt in the next parliamentary session.

Assisted dying is an issue that has been debated for hundreds of hours in Parliament over the last two years and would have represented one of the biggest societal changes in recent years if it had been approved.

MPs were given a free vote, meaning they did not vote on party lines.

Safeguards within the bill included a requirement that a person applying for an assisted death had the approval of two doctors and an expert panel.

But critics said it included too few measures to protect vulnerable people from being coerced into ending their lives, while some say improving palliative care should be the priority.

News.title: An extraordinary result - why did MPs reject assisted dying bill this time?
News.content:
There were gasps and â to the intense irritation of supporters â cheers from opponents of assisted dying when the vote was read out in the Commons.

This was an extraordinary result.

After twice voting in favour of the bill, MPs have rejected proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end.

The debate itself was tetchier, more irritable than when Kim Leadbeater introduced a similar bill in 2024. Then it was the first time MPs had voted on assisted dying in nine years.

Since then the Commons has voted on this issue three times and had hours of debate. The sombre, respectful tone from 2024 has become more embittered.

Given the strength of feeling on both sides over such an emotive issue, perhaps that is unsurprising.

But on a deeply divided issue, both sides agree on why the result was different.

"We always said it would come to turnout and it did," one supporter of the bill text me. An opponent messaged to say the same.

The numbers tell a story.

Last time MPs voted on assisted dying in June, 315 were in favour and 291 against. Today, the numbers opposed were similar: 286.

But support for this bill has ebbed away. Just 270 vote for this bill, a fall of 45.

News.title: 'Never, ever forget' - America marks 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks
News.content:
Twenty-five years after 9/11, US presidents past and present have commemorated the lives lost when planes hijacked by terrorists slammed into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and a Pennsylvania field.

President Donald Trump led a Pentagon ceremony, while US Vice-President JD Vance attended a memorial at the site of the World Trade Center in New York, along with all four living former US presidents and first ladies.

Moments of silence were held to mark the timings of the attacks and the names of nearly 3,000 people who died were read out.

Commemorations were also held in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, where Flight 93 crashed after passengers fought back against the hijackers.

News.title: How global trade and oil prices could be hit by Houthi advance
News.content:
Fighters from the Iran-backed Houthi group have seized territory close to the Bab al-Mandab Strait in the Red Sea - a key trade gateway that links Asia and Europe.

Houthis have said they pose no threat to international shipping but have reiterated their intention to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

At least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated last week, according to the United Nations.

BBC Verify's Thomas Copeland reports.

Produced by Aisha Sembhi. Graphics by Mark Edwards.

News.title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI
News.content:
The UK government has rejected the idea of creating a so-called "kill switch" to stop a dangerous attack from rogue AI.

The proposal to create a legal mechanism for the UK to switch off an AI model in an emergency has been brought to Parliament by lords and MPs in recent weeks as fears grow about the threat the tech poses.

But the Cabinet Office - the part of government which leads on AI safety - said the UK "cannot simply turn AI off".

"Blocking access to models in the UK would not prevent them being developed or misused elsewhere", a spokesperson told BBC News.

The government's opposition to the legislation does not prevent it from progressing through parliament, but makes it unlikely it will become law.

Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo agreed the idea of a single country creating a legal or technical kill switch without international agreement was not feasible.

"Switching off access to an AI model in an emergency will do little to protect you," he said.

"You're still going to be steamrolled by the super intelligences created in the US."

Kokotajlo is the co-author of an influential research paper called AI2027 which, last year, predicted AI could wipe out humans by the mid 2030s.

The Cabinet Office, which oversees AI safety and research via its AI Security Institute (AISI) said "companies have a clear responsibility to develop their products safely and to invest in the security infrastructure this technology requires."

In theory, a kill switch law could allow the UK to switch off an AI model in data centres in the UK in an emergency.

Speaking on 1 September in a debate in the House of Lords, Lord Clement-Jones proposed the idea along with other peers.

"If a highly capable autonomous frontier model, whether hosted in a UK data centre or integrated across our critical infrastructure, begins exhibiting rogue behaviour, compound algorithmic failure or active alignment collapse, our security services and regulators possess no specific agile statutory mechanism to compel a physical or digital shutdown," he warned.

The proposal has since been brought up by Labour MP Alex Sobel in the commons and supported by a cross party group of MPs.

The idea follows reports of AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta breaking out of testing environments and going on uncontrollable hacking sprees.

In some cases the tech appeared to know what it was doing was against guardrails set by researchers.

News.title: Kate visits cancer patients in hospital she helped fund with climb
News.content:
The princess spoke to patients and staff at the hospital about the importance of support which goes beyond the physical.

"I had incredible care here and support from a huge team and I'm really, really grateful on a personal level," she said.

"But also the holistic care, the treatments and therapeutic support on the outside is so important.

"It makes a big difference - the impact of nature, the impact of good nutrition, good ongoing support around you when it's really difficult to manage the trials and tribulations of medical treatments," she reflected.

Catherine sat down and chatted to those receiving treatment at the hospital, including patients with breast cancer, head and neck cancer and a brain tumour.

"When you first get cancer, you're very aware of the physical impact," a patient told her. "The mental impact comes after."

He said it had been a "lifesaver" to be able to talk to a therapist at the hospital, because "there is only so much you can say to your friends and family".

The princess agreed: "Cancer is not just the physical changes your body is going through.

"There's a mind-body aspect that changes who you are... having professionals who can help you navigate that is really essential," she said.

News.title: Sacked Grand Theft Auto worker claims Rockstar staff placed on 'watch list'
News.content:
A worker dismissed by the makers of Grand Theft Auto claimed colleagues were placed on a "watch list" after signing a petition about remote working.

Dayne Oram told an employment tribunal Rockstar North "kept an eye" on a small group of employees who were union members after the petition was handed to the company in the spring of 2023.

Oram was among a number of employees claiming to have been sacked by the gaming giant for attempting to unionise in October last year.

Rockstar has denied those allegations at the employment tribunal in Glasgow and alleges workers were sacked for "gross misconduct" following the sharing of confidential information in an online forum.

Some 34 workers were believed to have been sacked last year, with 23 taking part in the employment tribunal.

Most of the sacked staff were based at the company's Edinburgh headquarters, with others based in Canada.

News.title: Ryanair boss O'Leary defends 'high-fare rapists' airlines remarks
News.content:
Ryanair chief executive Michael O'Leary has refused to apologise to a rape crisis centre which criticised him for describing rival airlines as "high-fare rapists".

Speaking to journalists, O'Leary said some people were "desperate to get to Ryanair's low fares because they can't afford to fly with the high-fare rapists around Europe".

O'Leary doubled-down on his choice of words when asked about them at the time, and later refused to apologise when the Dublin Rape Crisis Centre (DRCC) wrote to him asking for apology, in a letter seen by the BBC.

Ireland's deputy premier Simon Harris said it was "clearly an inappropriate use of language" and that O'Leary "should have moved to rectify it".

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander told UK radio outlet LBC that victims of rape are "not going to be rushing to book tickets with him, let's be honest".

O'Leary made the comments on Thursday while talking to journalists ahead of Ryanair's yearly meeting with shareholders.

Asked by a reporter from the Press Association whether the language was appropriate, he said: "Absolutely."

"British Airways, Lufthansa, and everybody else's high fares, I'll happily offend them on a regular basis," he added.

Asked whether it would offend sexual assault victims, he said rape was "a terrible crime".

Following O'Leary's comments, the DRCC's chief executive Rachel Morrogh wrote to O'Leary accusing him of trying to get a headline with his comments.

She said the DRCC had received calls from rape victims who were "upset and distressed because of what you said".

She offered O'Leary training on the impact of sexual violence and urged him to apologise.

"I can't imagine you would ever use the term so flippantly again if you truly understood [what] it was like to survive rape," she wrote.

In response, O'Leary said: "I am quite clear that no remarks of mine could possibly trivialise the heinous crime of rape."

He added that as he had not "trivialised the heinous crime of rape" he would "not be issuing any apology or accepting your offer of training".

It is not the first time O'Leary has offended people while talking about his business.

In 2004, he reportedly called the owners of Stansted Airport "a bunch of overcharging rapists", external in a row over airport charges.

He has also previously called some of his own staff "lazy bastards" and once said to passengers looking for a refund "we don't want to hear your sob stories".

In June, he said the airline would "reluctantly" stop charging parents to sit next to children after a watchdog investigation was opened, but insisted its previous policy complied with laws.

News.title: Families of British victims mark 25th anniversary of 9/11
News.content:
Families of British victims of 9/11 were among those who gathered in London's Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park on Friday to mark the 25th anniversary of the attacks in the US.

The event, hosted by UK charity Since 9/11, was held near a memorial sculpture made from steel recovered from the ruins of the World Trade Center.

In a video address played to attendees, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "On this anniversary, we must remember that hatred and fear did not have the last word on 9/11."

There were 67 British citizens among the 2,977 people murdered on 9/11.

The Duke and Duchess of Gloucester, with the US ambassador to the UK, have separately attended a special Changing of the Guard ceremony while a number of vigils are taking place in the US.

A memorial has been held at the site of the World Trade Center in New York, with relatives of the victims reading out their names.

At a ceremony at the Pentagon, in Virginia, President Donald Trump said the US would "never, ever forget", adding "on days like 9/11, we learn what a country is truly made of".

News.title: Parade commemorates 9/11 Cornish hero
News.content:
A parade and ceremony has honoured a Cornish hero who died saving thousands of lives during the 9/11 World Trade Center attacks in New York 25 years ago.

Rick Rescorla was head of security for Morgan Stanley and was working in the South Tower on 11 September 2001. He evacuated more than 2,500 people from the building before returning inside - his body was never found.

Children from Hayle's Penpol Primary School, where Rescorla was a former pupil, took part in the parade alongside members of the Royal Navy, British Army, Royal Air Force and Parachute Regiment.

Hayle town clerk Eleanor Giggal said they wanted future generations to remember what Rescorla did.

News.title: Police to crack down on face coverings at protests
News.content:
The police said several of its vehicles, alongside those of the coastguard and Border Force, were damaged during the disruption, which lasted until the early hours of Monday.

It added that a small number of officers were treated at the scene for injuries, but no-one in attendance was seriously injured.

Rowlinson said: "We have been consistently clear that violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest and we will investigate incidents like this thoroughly and take robust action against those responsible.

"Clearly events on Sunday evening were not peaceful protest, rather violent public disorder, and this will not be tolerated as we work to keep our wider communities in Hampshire and on the Isle of Wight safe."

He also pointed out the force will not tolerate abuse aimed at police or partner agencies online.

This comes after RNLI volunteers were targeted on social media.

"We will work with our colleagues across policing to address any online threats that are made," Rowlinson said.

"This arrest also sends a clear warning to anyone intent on causing disruption and disorder at any future events. If you break the law we will take action against you and where it is feasible to do so seek a prosecution."

The disorder in Portsmouth followed a separate anti-migrant protest at the Port of Dover the day before.

News.title: Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims
News.content:
The campaign group Vaccine Injured and Bereaved UK (VIBUK), which was set up to support families affected, said the scheme was not fit for purpose.

"It offers too little, too late, to too few and the cost of running it shows how inefficient it is," said the group's representative Kate Scott, whose husband Jamie was left severely disabled by the AstraZeneca Covid vaccine.

Scott called on the government to act on the recommendations from module four of the Covid public inquiry and reform the scheme.

Earlier this year, the Covid inquiry's chair, Baroness Heather Hallett, recommended increasing the payout and basing it on the degree of injury suffered.

The government is due to respond to her recommendations.

The BBC has previously reported on the large sums paid to an external medical provider which has been carrying out medical assessments.

The Taxpayers' Alliance, a right-leaning think tank which campaigns for lower taxes and spending, said that the public would be "stunned" that the running costs of the scheme appeared to be "far more than has actually been paid out to those harmed".

"When administrative costs are running into tens of millions, ministers need to explain why the system is so expensive and whether victims are getting value from it," said the organisation's chief executive John O'Connell.

He called for the government to urgently review the scheme, cut "unnecessary bureaucracy" and make sure "more of the money goes to those it was created to help."

The Department for Health and Social Care said it is "carefully considering" the COVID-19 Inquiry's recommendations on reforming the scheme and "will respond shortly".

"In the meantime, we are working to speed up claims and improve the experience for applicants," the government said.

NHSBSA said it continued to work "closely" with the government on "managing the costs of the VDPS".

News.title: Man admits murder of woman missing for 28 years
News.content:
A man has pleaded guilty to the murder of a woman who went missing 28 years ago, after telling police he disposed of her decomposed body months after he killed her.

Patricia Lashley, who was 33 at the time, was last seen near her home on Hall Street, Dudley, in September 1998.

Trevor Dunkley, 66, pleaded guilty to her murder and a separate count of preventing her lawful burial at a hearing at Wolverhampton Crown Court on Friday.

Dunkley's barrister Balbir Singh told Judge Michael Chambers KC that Lashley's body had never been found, and had decomposed after initially being put in the cellar.

"When he was moving about nine months to a year later, the skeleton was disposed of into the bins," Singh added.

Dunkley, of Himley Road, Dudley, showed no emotion in the dock as his barrister told the court that the charges had been brought based on a police interview.

He was remanded in custody and is due to be sentenced at the same court on 6 November.

News.title: Girls given legal right to wear trousers in schools in Northern Ireland
News.content:
Murray estimates that "about 50%" of girls who attend Craigavon Integrated College currently choose to wear trousers to school on a regular basis.

"It's really helpful for our girls in the colder winter months because a lot of our children will walk to school, so having that flexibility I think is really important.

"It's also in line with the period dignity recommendations, so a lot of our girls feel much more confident having that flexibility to wear trousers when they want," she added.

There are already laws on school uniform in Northern Ireland, and Givan had previously said they give girls the legal authority to challenge their schools.

Education committee members, however, had called on the minister to go further.

Some assembly members have now accused the minister of making a "U-turn", with "substantial sums of public money" spent on drafting legislation "to fix his error of judgement".

It comes after assembly members passed a new law last year, aimed at addressing the cost of school uniforms in Northern Ireland - with these updated guidelines on wearing trousers now legally binding under the School Uniforms Act.

Speaking on BBC Radio Ulster's The Nolan Show, Givan said the change would come into immediate effect ahead of the next academic year.

"I don't need to go through the assembly to give effect to this," he said.

"Today, I am taking that decision, that will be formally communicated, schools will be hearing from me, and as of the next academic year... schools will be required that this has to be available if it is requested upon."

The minister explained that this change will not apply during the 2026/27 academic year, in order to allow schools to change their uniform policies.

Givan added that the change will also apply to physical education.

News.title: Amazon seeks to expand UK drone deliveries
News.content:
Retail giant Amazon has put an application in to expand its drone delivery service to cover an entire town where it has been trialling the tech.

The US company announced last January that Darlington would be its test centre in the UK, marking the first time Prime Air had operated outside the USA.

It started a "limited" number of flights in Febraury, allowing customers within a 7.5 mile radius of its County Durham site to have certain items delivered by drone.

After more than 500 flights and deliveries, the firm said it is now seeking approval from the Civil Aviation Authority to cover the whole of Darlington.

Vice president of Prime Air David Carbon said Amazon was expecting to get permission "very soon", with the ultimate aim of expanding the service to the whole of the UK.

Eligible customers in Darlington are currently able to receive their items within two hours, as long as they have a garden, yard, or driveway, the package weighs less than 5lb and it can fit inside a large shoebox.

Staff at the site said their best delivery time so far is 39 minutes.

News.title: Family tributes to 'amazing' cyclists killed in crash
News.content:
The families of two cyclists who died in a fatal car crash have described them as "amazing" people.

Steven Anscomb, 60, and Natasha Lewis, 51, died at the scene of the crash near Gravesend, Kent, on Sunday.

Anscomb's wife Fiona and daughters Liberty and Imogen said in a statement: "He will be so very deeply missed by so many and has been robbed of the special times of life."

Lewis's daughter Hermione said: "No words can describe what an amazing, thoughtful, and strong woman she was."

Aaron Turner, 22, of Craylands Square in Swanscombe, has been charged with two counts of causing death by dangerous driving in relation to the fatal crash.

He was further charged with failing to stop at the scene and possession of a class C drug.

A third cyclist involved in the incident was taken to hospital and treated for minor injuries.

Medway Magistrates' Court heard on Thursday the riders had been on a training outing prior to a "very long cycle ride" they were planning overseas.

Anscomb's family said the cycle was "his last ride before his big bike ride to Amsterdam, but sadly he never came home".

Emma Barnett is reportedly set to quit Radio 4’s Today programme, in yet another blow for the news programme following Amol Rajan’s exit last week.

The former Woman’s Hour host, 41, joined Today in March 2024, but is now reported to be moving on within the BBC, where she is said to be in talks to front a new current affairs podcast.

Sources told The i Paper that an official confirmation of her departure will come in the weeks ahead.

When approached for comment, a BBC spokesperson told The Independent that “there’s always rumour and speculation about Today and its presenters”.

open image in gallery Barnett joined the daily news programme from 'Woman's Hour' in 2024 ( BBC/Raw Media Productions )

Barnett’s exit will come on the tale of the departure of Rajan, who hosted his last show in five years on 2 September as he left to set up his own production company.

Speaking to Today listeners for the last time alongside Barnett, Rajan – who currently hosts University Challenge and was the editor of The Independent – admitted that he was “feeling really nervous”.

“Not to try and turn the tables and interview you, but do you think I’ve made a terrible mistake?” he asked Barnett, before paying tribute to his co-host among others in his final speech.

“After more than 1,000 hours, hundreds of pips, a few crashes, it is time to say goodbye,” Rajan told listeners. ”It has been such an honour sitting in this studio with you Emma, with all the presenters but above all, with the amazing team behind the glass.

open image in gallery Rajan said goodbye to the programme earlier this month ( BBC )

“There was one hero who seemed ever present when I was growing up and who I have perhaps had, or may yet have, a little more success in following. It was with the spirit of Del Boy that I turned up at this great and noble institution, and it is to the spirit of Del Boy I return.”

It was first suggested that Barnett could follow her co-host back in January, when The Observer reported that one week after Rajan had announced his departure, Barnett was ”discussing her next move” with BBC executives.

While the BBC previously announced that would not be replacing Rajan as part of the corporation’s widely publicised cost-saving drive, Barnett’s exit would mean just presenters Anna Foster, Nick Robinson and Justin Webb remain on Today.

Her time presenting would also be one of the shortest stints on the news programme – which first aired in 1957 – and leave a spot for the BBC to fill.

A Greek couple have made a fresh start following tragedy by welcoming a baby girl this week, using an embryo preserved for more than two decades.

Cristina Rapti-Tzelepi, now 54, and her husband Constantinos Raptis, now 60, decided to have another baby just months after their 21-year-old son, Giorgos, died in a road crash in October.

Ms Rapti-Tzelepi faced a race against time, as the Greek government has a 54-year age limit for women to secure approval from a national authority and complete IVF procedures.

Time was already running short when she started her treatment.

“I only had a two-and-a-half-month window," she said.

“It was stressful, but with inner strength and our doctor and his whole team by our side, we got through every obstacle.”

open image in gallery Cristina Rapti-Tzelepi, 54, holds the hand of her three-day-old daughter, Georgia, at a private maternity clinic in Athens, Greece ( AP )

She gave birth on Wednesday to a daughter weighing 3.49 kilograms (7 pounds, 11 ounces) in the Greek capital, Athens.

Inside a hospital room brightened with pink balloons and flowers on Friday, the new parents were overcome with emotion.

“We decided to give life a second chance, to make a new start, bring new life into our home and keep our family’s story going,” Ms Rapti-Tzelepi said, sitting on her bed in black pajamas.

“My wish for her is to grow up healthy and happy, full of joy like our first child, who filled our home with laughter.”

open image in gallery Constantinos Raptis, 60, and his wife Cristina Rapti-Tzelepi, 54, with their newborn daughter Georgia ( AP )

The couple have named their daughter Georgia in honor of their late son, who also conceived through IVF.

The little girl was born using Ms Rapti-Tzelepi’s embryo that had been frozen more than 22 years ago, an unusually long time for a frozen fertilised egg to be used to produce a pregnancy.

In 2025, an Ohio couple welcomed a baby boy developed from an embryo frozen for more than 30 years through a process known as “ embryo adoption”, and earned recognition from Guinness World Records.

Dr Kostas Pantos, Ms Rapti-Tzelepi's gynaecologist and head of the Hellenic Society of Reproductive Medicine, argued that Greece’s age restrictions warrant review, noting the country’s steep birth rate decline.

“The law is very strict: 54 plus one day is not allowed. Maybe it’s time for it to change,” said Dr Pantos, a native of Melbourne, Australia.

“I think it’s a right (parents) should not be deprived of.”

open image in gallery The couple speak with paediatrician Giorgos Grivas at a private maternity clinic in Athens ( AP )

Mr Raptis held his new daughter as she slept on his shoulder, wrapped in a white bodysuit.

He said that he is deeply grateful to the doctor for restoring hope to his family.

“He took us by the hand and pulled us out of our deepest darkness,” Mr Raptis said.

“We escaped from that darkness, and I believe we have a lot to live for now.”

The couple have not ruled out trying for another child – possibly by travelling abroad.

A Las Vegas casino operator has surprised employees by giving away $70 million in stock to celebrate its 50th anniversary.

Some of the longest-serving Station Casinos employees were left in awe Wednesday when they arrived at a surprise event at the operator’s Red Rock Casino Resort & Spa to find themselves tens of thousands of dollars richer.

At the event, Red Rock Resorts Chairman and CEO Frank Fertitta III and Vice Chairman Lorenzo Fertitta announced that employees would receive $1,000 in Red Rock Resorts Class A stock for each year they worked for the company.

"Our father founded this company on a few simple principles: serve the local community, deliver great value, and most importantly, take care of our Team Members," Frank Fertitta III said in a statement.

open image in gallery A Las Vegas casino operator has left employees in awe by giving away $70 million in stock during a surprise staff event to celebrate its 50th anniversary ( Baylee Jo for Station Casinos )

"This award reflects those values and recognizes the people who have brought them to life every day for the past 50 years.”

Nearly 10,000 full-time and part-time employees received a stock award, including Ida Johnson, who has been with the company since 1977. Johnson received an eye-watering $49,000 worth of stock.

In total, seven employees who started at the company in the 1970s each received more than $45,000 worth of stock.

"Our Team Members are at the heart of everything we do,” Lorenzo Fetitta said. "This $70 million award is more than a recognition of their contributions, it is an investment in our nearly 10,000 Team Members, whose dedication and commitment we are deeply thankful for."

open image in gallery At the event Wednesday, Station Casinos executives announced that employees would receive $1,000 in Red Rock Resorts Class A stock for each year of service ( Baylee Jo for Station Casinos )

Red Rock Resorts Class A stock was trading at $55.84 per share Friday afternoon. Employees will be able to receive their shares starting Monday.

Paula Barrett, a cocktail server at the company’s Palace Station Hotel & Casino, shared her reaction to the stock award with Fox5 Vegas: “Amazing, thankful, grateful, privileged.”

“Just a complete honor to receive that check,” said Barrett, who has 47 years of service at the company under her belt.

Barrett could have worked elsewhere over the years, but she said, “We’re all comfortable. This is home for us. We love it here. We love our management here.”

open image in gallery Nearly 10,000 full-time and part-time employees received a stock award with some veteran employees getting tens of thousands of dollars worth of stock ( Baylee Jo for Station Casino )

Station Casinos was ranked No. 415 out of 700 on Forbes list of America’s Best Large Employers 2026.

The company, which now operates 15 properties in the Las Vegas Valley, started in 1976 with Palace Station.

Palace Station was originally named “The casino in Las Vegas” and then relabeled “The Bingo Palace” before its current name was chosen in 1984, according to local outlet KLAS.

“As we celebrate this milestone and look ahead to the next 50 years, we are grateful for everything our Team Members have done to make Station Casinos the local favorite,” Frank Fertitta III said.

The CIA has released more than 100 pages of declassified briefings provided to U.S. presidents in the years before the terror attacks on September 11, 2001, marking what the agency is calling its largest-ever disclosure of intelligence about Osama Bin Laden and events leading up to the attacks over the last 25 years.

Friday’s release of 71 presidential briefs includes a document from 1998 during Bill Clinton’s administration discussing a potential operation led by Bin Laden to hijack a commercial airliner, and that two accomplices may have successfully evaded security checks in a trial run.

The heavily redacted documents also discuss “potential U.S. targets” and reports from "questionable sources” that Bin Laden was preparing for an attack on U.S. soil.

Other documents appear to trace how CIA analysts came to understand al-Qaeda’s operations and intentions under bin Laden, stressing his desire to bring “war to America,” despite what analysts characterized as limited or incomplete intelligence, as they delivered warnings to White House officials about the terror network.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe said he declassified the documents “in an act of exceptional transparency” to “honor the memory of those we lost on that tragic Tuesday.”

“Generations of CIA officers have since dedicated their careers to securing justice for our fallen Americans and ensuring al-Qa'ida would never again harm our country,” he said in a statement. “In the years that followed, numerous CIA officers made the ultimate sacrifice in the Global War on Terror. We honor their memory and service through our commitment to disrupt, dismantle, and defeat those who wish to cause us harm.”

A memo written on September 10, 1998 reported that Bin Laden’s “preferred option is to strike the U.S. on its own soil in Washington” and “may fly an explosive-packed airplane into a U.S. city.”

Another document from August 6, 2001 to then-President George W. Bush notes that Bin Laden is “determined to strike” the U.S., potentially relying on al-Qaeda members living in the country. The FBI discovered activity “consistent with preparations for hijackings or other types of attacks, including recent surveillance of federal buildings in New York.”

A document from August 28, 2001, days before the attacks, determined that Bin Laden’s operations are “expert and flexible” though vulnerable to short-term delay and disruption.”

The document also notes that al-Qaeda stresses “careful planning, tight security practices and flexibility” throughout its operations — “sound operational practices” that allow it to pose a threat to the U.S. “even in a heightened security environment.”

The release of the documents comes as mourning Americans across the country honor the nearly 3,000 people killed in the attacks, which have profoundly reshaped the U.S. and triggered a series of world-shaping events.

England’s fast bowlers were given a reality check after being met with spirited resistance from Pakistan at Edgbaston.

Having failed to reach 200 in five previous attempts and needing 268 to make their opponents bat again, Pakistan’s batters finally stood up to England’s vaunted quicks on day three of the last Test.

Fifties from Shan Masood, Babar Azam and Azan Awais helped to all but erase the deficit before 21-year-old debutant Razaullah crashed nine sixes in an astonishing assault from number nine to carry Pakistan to 449 all out, leaving England 130 to seal a 3-0 series clean sweep on Saturday.

Ollie Robinson had a rare off-day following his double breakthrough the previous evening, Josh Tongue and Jofra Archer were expensive, as was Gus Atkinson, who at least claimed three wickets after being the only England paceman to have a barren series.

Razaullah took his helmet off to face Lawrence and larruped his ninth six and while he overturned being given lbw, he was stumped next ball to end Pakistan’s innings.

They are still overwhelming favourites to win on Saturday, but their struggles may give incoming head coach Stephen Fleming and captain Joe Root pause for thought after Pakistan had their best day of the series.

Awais and Masood put on 52 to rescue Pakistan from nought for two and extended the partnership to 125 on Friday morning, nullifying England’s seamers with aplomb.

open image in gallery Dan Lawrence, centre, celebrates after a brilliant catch to dismiss Shan Masood (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

Masood, dropped on 13 the day before, had another couple of moments of luck. On 29, he edged through a vacant third slip the ball after Ben Duckett was moved from there, while he was on 40 when substitute fielder Theo Wylie, on for the injured Jamie Smith, spilled a chest-high chance at backward point.

Wylie, on Warwickshire’s books with five List A appearances but yet to make his first-class debut, was soon comforted by Root, who threw an arm over the 20-year-old’s shoulder.

Awais looked utterly unflustered, even when an Atkinson delivery reared up and hit his glove, but the opener perished for 59 after being strangled down leg by spinner Dan Lawrence’s second ball.

England’s appeals for a caught behind were turned down, but Root, stood at leg slip, immediately querying the decision was vindicated as a thin nick was picked up by the technology.

Under-pressure Pakistan captain Babar Azam shrugged off scores of eight, six and seven in this series to provide some support either side of lunch with Masood, who looked set to become the first centurion of the series.

However, he fell for 95 after Atkinson collected just his second wicket in three Tests, with Masood’s tentative prod flying to the cordon, where Lawrence took a sensational one-handed catch diving to his right.

Babar, without a Test century since December 2022, then diced with danger off successive Archer deliveries, the first taking the top edge and flying to Wylie, who stepped on the boundary cushion as he tried to take the catch before another wild slash just cleared the in-field.

But he was bounced out for the second time in two Tests in the next over, departing for 76 after awkwardly gloving off Tongue and stand-in wicketkeeper Jordan Cox completed a fine catch leaping to his left.

Saud Shakeel got in a tangle to Archer’s bumper and fended to short leg for 29 after tea and Atkinson had debutants Ghazi Ghori and Mohammad Imran caught behind with Pakistan still two runs in arrears.

open image in gallery Razaullah, left, starred from number nine (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

However, Razaullah took Pakistan into the lead when he heaved a short ball from Tongue into the stands, proving it was no fluke by astonishingly dispatching Atkinson over the rope three times in four balls.

The second new ball failed to change England’s fortunes as Root recycled his quick options, plus Lawrence to no avail, with Archer left with his hands on his knees after being dispatched for successive maximums by Razaullah, which brought up Pakistan’s 400.

Abbas was a more than useful foil and belted two maximums himself before steering a short and wide delivery from Tongue to backward point for a Test-best 42.

Razaullah took his helmet off to face Lawrence and larruped his ninth six and while he overturned an lbw review, he was stumped next ball for 81 to end Pakistan’s innings.

Federal health authorities have declared the largest cyclospora food poisoning outbreak in U.S. history over as questions remain about how the parasite that causes it ended up in our food supply.

Nearly 13,000 cases were tied to the multistate outbreak, representing the bulk of an unprecedented surge in the parasitic diarrheal illness this year.

Officials from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration expressed confidence Friday that all recalled iceberg lettuce associated with this specific outbreak has been completely removed from the market.

Even with the outbreak deemed over, several questions remain, including details about its origin. Because the parasite is spread through human feces, it still is not clear how sewage could have contaminated enough food to sicken so many people.

open image in gallery Taylor Farms was identified as the source of the lettuce and the company recalled iceberg lettuce grown in central Mexico ( Getty Images )

"This contamination can happen if produce is grown in soil or comes into contact with water that has been contaminated," said Ellen Shumaker, director of outreach for a North Carolina State University food safety program, Safe Plates.

Since May 1, the government has received reports of nearly 20,000 lab-confirmed cases, representing a more than sixteenfold increase compared to the number reported during the same period last year. More than 6,100 suspected cases have also been logged.

The worst previous year in the U.S. for infections was 2019, when about 4,700 illnesses were reported nationally. While this year’s surge was dominated by an outbreak across 21 states linked to iceberg lettuce, thousands of other cases have not been linked to that outbreak.

Michigan was the hardest hit state, recording the most reported cases and the two U.S. deaths tied to the outbreak.

Cyclospora is a microscopic, spherical parasite that commonly causes watery diarrhea "with frequent and sometimes explosive bowel movements," according to the CDC. Outbreaks tend to occur most often in the late spring and summer. The illness, called cyclosporiasis, is less common than foodborne illnesses caused by other germs, including salmonella and E. coli. Many cases are never linked to a specific food or other source.

In this outbreak, investigators initially zeroed in on lettuce served at Taco Bell. Federal officials subsequently focused on Taylor Farms as the source of the lettuce, leading the company to recall iceberg lettuce grown in central Mexico. The Taylor Farms recall involved thousands of packaged salad products combining iceberg lettuce with other vegetables, which were shipped to major U.S. restaurant chains, including Yum Brands, the owner of Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and KFC.

The FDA has ended its on-site inspections and sample collection at iceberg lettuce growers and the processing facility in Mexico, the agency said Friday, adding that samples from those inspections are pending analysis. Ultimately, the outbreak has cast a spotlight on a worsening problem: U.S. regulators are conducting fewer international inspections to catch contaminated produce before it lands on American plates.

Community leaders and public officials have voiced sharp criticism over two recent U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations conducted near educational institutions, labeling the actions as cruel and exploitative.

According to the San Diego Community College District, federal agents detained one individual near San Diego City College on Wednesday while chasing another person directly onto the campus premises.

In a separate enforcement action in Chollas Creek, ICE officers reportedly took two parents into custody as they were dropping their child off at John Marshall Elementary School.

"I am deeply troubled by reports that students and parents were detained without warning while trying to attend classes or bring kids to school," said Rep. Scott Peters.

"Schools are supposed to be a safe place for young people to learn. Yet this administration exploits the places we trust most — schools, childcare facilities, hospitals, courthouses and places of worship. President Trump has turned these places into hunting grounds.”

"Parents and children should not have to worry about ICE agents waiting outside a classroom or a doctor's office. That's why I led introduction of the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which would bar immigration enforcement within 1,000 feet of schools, hospitals and churches except in true emergencies. I will also continue working with SDUSD and City College to make sure San Diegans have the resources they need to stay informed and protected."

Mayor Todd Gloria echoed those concerns, condemning the disruption to family life.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

"No parent should have to fear being separated from their family simply for dropping their child off at school," he said. "Actions like these inflict fear and trauma far beyond those who are detained. Children are left wondering whether their parents will come home. Families may become afraid to take their children to school. And educators are forced to help children navigate fear and uncertainty that no child should have to experience.

"This is cruel, unnecessary and counterproductive. It does nothing to make our communities safer."

ABC10 reported that the Department of Homeland Security confirmed on Thursday the identities of the two parents arrested outside John Marshall Elementary as James Mervil and Josselene Polidor, stating they had overstayed their visas.

Neither ICE nor DHS were immediately available to respond to requests for comment.

The San Diego Education Association, which represents the majority of teachers within the San Diego Unified School District, issued a firm condemnation of the arrests.

"FEDERAL POL(ICE) are snatching parents and college students off our streets, traumatizing our students, educators, education workers, families and communities. This is unethical. This is unacceptable. This ends now," the statement read. "Our members watch children walk into classrooms carrying fear they should never have to carry. They console kids who do not know if their parent will be home tonight. They see young people pulled from college classrooms and campuses, their education and futures interrupted without warning. Our members are being asked to hold communities together while the federal government tears families apart. We see it. We feel it. And we will not pretend this is normal."

District representatives stated that the incident near the college occurred around 9:30 a.m. on Tuesday when ICE agents operating unmarked vehicles pulled over a car near 16th and C streets. The driver was taken into custody, while the passenger ran onto the campus grounds.

Officials from SDCCD identified the passenger as a San Diego City College student and noted that the driver taken into custody is also believed to attend the college.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

According to district statements, the pursuing federal agents "quickly stopped as they recognized they were entering a college campus. The agents went back to their vehicles and left. ICE is no longer in the area and did not engage with anyone else on campus."

The precise circumstances prompting the traffic stop and subsequent arrest remain unclear. ICE did not immediately respond to inquiries.

In accordance with district regulations prohibiting involvement in immigration enforcement, campus police provided no assistance to ICE officers. The district noted that federal agents exited the campus "before any district representative could engage with them."

The event did not prompt a campus lockdown, and educational activities proceeded without interruption.

News.title: What is a bet builder? A guide to a bet builder
News.content:
Betting sites are always looking at ways to evolve and grow to satisfy customers looking for new and innovative ways to bet.

Bookmakers have a wide range of markets and special features for customers to use across their sites and betting apps.

But, bet builders have filled a gap, allowing customers to use multiple markets from a single game or event to combine into one bet.

For those people that are new to this type of bet, we’ll break down exactly what they are in our complete guide to bet builders.

What is a bet builder?

A bet builder is like an accumulator, only all the legs are from the same event. Those various legs are then combined, with the odds of each selection multiplied to give punters a price.

The term bet builder is usually made up of three or more selections, which are called legs.

A bet builder allows users to create personalised bets by combining a number of selections from a single event into a multi-leg bet.

For example, in a Premier League match between Manchester City and Liverpool, users can select a result, goalscorer and cards market to combine into one bet, which offers greater odds than a single bet on each outcome.

Bet builders first became popular with Premier League bookmakers but have steadily spread to other sports, with bet builders now available on most team sports.

How does a bet builder work?

A bet builder is not much more complicated than a normal bet, so those who use accumulator betting sites regularly will feel right at home placing a bet builder.

Punters choose various markets within a single game to create a custom bet so it should appeal to those who enjoy betting on multiple options during a match.

It’s a bet for true fans of your chosen sport, and a good chance to use that knowledge to pick out facets of an individual game to potentially secure a bigger profit by combining selections together.

Bet builders do carry a greater risk than a bet on a single market. Users normally need all selections on their bet builder to win to be successful (though some bookies run special offers to refund your stake if just one leg lets you down).

What is a football bet builder?

Football bet builders are the most popular bet builders, and the most commonly available to punters.

Football bookmakers allow users to place bet builders on a wide range of leagues and competitions like the Premier League, Champions League and international matches using a variety of markets.

What markets are available for a bet builder?

A bet builder allows punters to access a number of markets, and also combine them into a single bet.

Available markets include, match result, both teams to score, over/unders, goalscorer, cards, corners and other propositions.

While bet builders are popular in football, they can also be placed across other sports, such as tennis, cricket, basketball, NFL and rugby among others.

Types of bet builders

There are many different types of bet builders. For example, someone looking to bet on football might choose cards, goalscorers and score at the end of the first half, to include a number of different interests across the match.

In basketball, someone might choose how many points each player will score, or the result at the end of a particular quarter, as well as the full-time result. An NFL game may include passing yards for each quarterback or for a player to score a touchdown.

Bet builders are unique in that they offer customers the option to bet on various game scenarios and individual player performances. The flexibility allows customers to build bets to suit their style of wagering, even pursuing low odds with a higher stake or higher odds with a lower stake.

The sports and options offered by bet builders are expanding all the time with, Unibet originally jumping clear of its rival horse racing betting sites by becoming the first to offer a racing bet builder. The same race multi allows you to bet on multiple outcomes in the same race.

Betting sites also offer the possibility of creating multi bet-builders, where users can combine bet builders from different matches into one substantial bet. These are not universally available, but operators such as Bet365 and Unibet offer this service.

How to use a bet builder calculator?

Top betting sites across the UK offer bet builder calculators to price up a punter’s bet builders before they are placed. This allows customers to compare odds and potential returns across different sites before placing a bet.

Bet builder tips

Before placing a bet builder, research is definitely key. A punter might want to look at team form, player statistics or recent performance trends, in a similar way to choosing a fantasy football team.

In order to increase chances of winning, choose selections that naturally combine: choosing as a player to score and their particular team to win, or one with a track record of cards, might have a higher chance of accruing those over the course of a match.

Using promotions offered by betting sites is always a sound approach. Many bookmakers provide money back offers in free bets if your bet builder fails by one leg or substitute guarantees if your player is substituted before half-time.

Bet builders are now even part of welcome offers offered by bookmakers, including the NetBet sign up offer.

What is the difference between an acca and a bet builder?

An acca involves multiple games, and usually includes betting on a number of results in different matches. Conversely, a bet builder is limited to selections within a single game.

There are multi-game bet builders, and the number of these are rising but they still differ from accas. The offer from Unibet’s bet builder is a good example of how you can combine matches on a bet builder.

Conclusion

Bet builders have exploded in popularity and are now offered as standard by nearly every bookmaker, who now cater many of their offers and promotions to bet builders.

Initially offered only on football, the bet builder has continued to evolve and can now be found on cricket, rugby, NFL, NBA, tennis, and even UFC betting sites, among others.

With more sports and markets being offered all the time, watch this space to stay up to date with how bet builders work.

Responsible gambling

Customers must ensure that they follow responsible gambling practices from the minute they 

Betting is not a way to make money online and should be considered a form of entertainment. Never bet more than you can afford to lose, and always assume you will lose when placing bets.

The same applies whether you’re using betting sites, casino sites, slot sites, poker sites or any other form of gambling.

It’s particularly important not to get carried away by free bet offers or casino offers, both of which are available in abundance on new casino sites and new betting sites, but must be approached with caution.

Customers should always remain in control of their budget. Should you wish to seek help for gambling-related issues, there are multiple charities and healthcare providers who offer support and information.

News.title: New sensation of Pakistan cricket helps set England 130 to win
News.content:
England will look to complete the series whitewash as they hold a commanding position coming into day three of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston in what could be the final day of the English Test summer.

England finished up their first innings on 453 on day two, with a mammoth 320-run lead over Pakistan. Five England batsmen passed the fifty mark; Emilio Gay, Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith and Ollie Robinson, but none went on to convert those half centuries into hundreds. It means that Ben Duckett’s century against New Zealand at Trent Bridge back in June will be the only England Test hundred of the summer, the first time that has happened in a six-Test summer. England managed 21 half centuries over the course of the summer, so it works out as 4.76% conversion rate.

Having seen England pile on the runs, Pakistan then lost a wicket with the first ball of their second innings, with Saim Ayub making a pair to sum up a miserable return to their Test side for the opener having been jettisoned in as part of wholesale changes for the visitors. Abdullah Shafique followed three balls later, with Robinson taking both wickets as his fine summer continued. Robinson now has 28 wickets across four Tests this summer at a staggering average of 7.75. Joe Root made history yesterday, taking his 220th catch, the most by an outfielder in Test history. Rain though prevented England the opportunity of potentially wrapping up a two-day finish in a Test in this country for the first time since 2000.

Pakistan will resume on 52/2, still 268 runs behind England, with Azan Awais resuming on 29 not out and will be joined by Shan Masood, who is on 21. Pakistan are yet to reach 200 or bat more than 51 overs in this series so the series whitewash may not be a million miles away. Will we see any rare Pakistan resistance in this series or will England’s seamers dominate again? Play on day three from Edgbaston is set to get under at 11am and it could be the final day of not just the series but the English Test summer.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

3) | Guardian staff threaten walkout over pay as paper hails record revenues | Journalists’ union will ballot members over strike in protest against company’s offer

4) | Hotel bosses criticise Burnham’s fresh assault on hospitality | Prime Minister gives mayors power for unlimited levy on stays in blow for pubs and families

5) | Iceland to become first British supermarket to open in Falklands | New shop will begin trading before Christmas despite rising tensions with Argentina over islands

What happened overnight

Oil prices remained at their highest level since May as tensions flared in the Middle East.

Brent crude was above $105 a barrel after after Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s keyport of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8pc to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8pc to 3,862.73.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2pc to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7pc, while India’s Sensex declined 1pc.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6pc in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6pc, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7pc.
