News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: ‘All I see are dead bodies’: The survivors of Syria’s chemical massacres
News.content:
“Unfortunately, I am still alive,” says Mohammed Suliaiman Abo Alkair, his green eyes heavy and distant.

The 38-year-old steps from his living room onto the roof and gestures towards a cluster of trees – a lone patch of green in a sea of grey rubble. It was there, at two in the morning 13 years ago that the whistle of a rocket ended not in an explosion but a thud.

For a moment, there was relief; the feeling of being spared. But then came a cloud of the nerve agent sarin.

Almost everyone around Mohammed died. His family and one small boy in a neighbouring house were the only ones to survive.

That August night, as Damascus slept, forces loyal to the Syrian President Bashar al-Assad launched eight sarin-filled rockets at the opposition-held districts of Zamalka, Ein Tarma and Jobar. The US government estimated that 1,429 people were killed, including 426 children. Other estimates put the number at 1729.

For more than a decade, nobody was held to account. Mr Assad denied the attack, shielded those responsible and later used sarin again – at Khan Sheikhoun in 2017, and in at least ten further attacks documented by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Only after Mr Assad fled Syria in December 2024 did the prospect of justice emerge. Investigators for Syria’s new government have since uncovered previously undeclared chemical-munitions caches, and the authorities have detained 18 suspects. None has yet been tried or punished.

But as attention turns at last to justice, the survivors remain invisible, absent from the reckoning. For now at least they remain largely invisible.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star who cost £80m in transfer fees now playing in front of 246 people for EFL side
Sports.content:
JUST three years ago, Aaron Ramsdale was starting regularly for Arsenal in the Premier League.

Now, he finds himself playing for Southampton in front of crowds of just 246 people.



Since returning to the Saints from his Newcastle loan, Ramsdale has been demoted to fourth-choice goalkeeper, behind Daniel Peretz, George Long and Jamie Jones.

The 28-year-old is yet to feature in a match for the first team this season, but played for the Under-21s in their Premier League Cup opener against Blackburn last month.



Less than 300 spectators turned out to watch the match at the Silverlake Stadium in Eastleigh.

Ramsdale kept a clean sheet as the Saints cruised to a 4-0 win.

It was his first appearance since April 18 – when he featured for Newcastle against Bournemouth in the Premier League.

Ramsdale made 23 appearances during his season-long loan with the Magpies and kept two clean sheets.

Newcastle had the opportunity to sign him for around £20million this summer, but rejected the move.

The Prem giants paid a £4m loan fee to get the goalkeeper to St James’ Park last August, taking the total amount in transfer fees over time for him up to just under £80m.

Sports.title: Man Utd coach Darren Fletcher clashes with ‘abusive’ fan outside Old Trafford after win over Sabah
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED coach Darren Fletcher bit back at a rowdy fan who was “abusive” after their Champions League win over Sabah.

United enjoyed a thumping return to European competition as they thrashed the Azerbaijani minnows 4-0.



But there were some unsavoury scenes after the game as United stars boarded their team bus home.

Fans had waited behind after full time to grab pictures and autographs.



According to the Daily Mail, Fletcher angered one supporter after failing to sign his autograph.

The former Scotland midfielder – who is now head coach of United’s Under-18s – had signed some autographs but wasn’t able to get to all the fans behind the bus.



And after hearing shouts in his direction, Fletcher was having none of it.

He hit back: “Hey, listen. It doesn’t matter, you can’t speak like that.

Fletcher, 42, then pointed at the angry supporter and said: “You are the reason people don’t sign. You are the reason people don’t sign.”

His stern response led to huge cheers from other United fans standing by the bus.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

One posted a clip of the exchange on X and pointed out how he “put a fan in his place” who was “abusive towards players when they didn’t stop”.

Another said: “What a man! Fair play Fletcher.”

A third added: “Always loved Darren Fletcher. Good on him.”



And a fourth said: “Love to see it.”

Fletcher is a United legend after appearing 342 times for the Red Devils, scoring 24 goals.

He won five Premier League titles under Sir Alex Ferguson and the Champions League.

Fletcher has been in the United coaching set-up since 2020 and initially worked as technical director before coaching the Under-16s and Under-18s.

He took charge of the team as interim boss for two games last season after Ruben Amorim was axed.

Fletcher then returned to his role as Under-18s boss where he coaches stars like JJ Gabriel.

Sports.title: How Man Utd can hurt Man City with their ‘postman’ strategy to thwart Enzo Maresca’s ‘clone rangers’
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED will be looking to expose a Manchester City weakness when the two rivals meet at Old Trafford on Sunday.

With Pep Guardiola now gone and Enzo Maresca having replaced him, the Sky Blues have adopted a slightly new approach to games.



It has worked in the Premier League so far, with City having won each of their opening three games.

But one area has appeared slightly vulnerable at time – and the Red Devils will seek to expose it with the help of a ‘bouncer’ move and a ‘postman’ strategy.



In the latest episode of SunSport’s Tactics Exposed, our tactics expert Dean Scoggins looks at how Man Utd can capitalise on City’s setup.

THE ‘BOUNCER’

Man Utd set up in a 4-2-3-1 – although they will probably slot into more of a 4-4-2 with Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha playing as the two highest players.



City also set up in a 4-2-3-1 but will push high in the game to a 3-1-6 shape.

Unlike the way Guardiola and Mikel Arteta approach a game, instead of a centre midfielder playing between the centre-backs in that attacking formation, the left-sided defender moves into the middle – in this case, it’s Josko Gvardiol, although with City it could be anyone – which allows Elliot Anderson to roam in midfield.

City can then hurt teams on the edge of the box through the likes of Enzo Fernandez, Rayan Cherki, Phil Foden etc.

Maresca has been building up with one in the middle, meaning the three players left in defence see a lot of the ball.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

However, that will give Man Utd a big opportunity to attack the wide spaces behind the defence with a ‘bouncer’ move, which could really hurt City.

With Marcus Rashford over on the left, instead of him being wide and stretching the pitch, United will want him moving inside slightly to keep the Man City defenders narrow.

Then, when Man Utd win the ball back, the England star can move wide again, giving the right-sided City defender a dilemma – follow him or stay narrow.

The same goes for Bryan Mbeumo on the right.

Porto exposed the space in the Man City midfield at times during the Champions League meeting between the two sides on Tuesday.



THE ‘POSTMAN’

Questions have been raised about United’s ‘false nine’ setup, and whether operating without a natural centre-forward is truly effective.

Against Everton, United struggled because they kept floating deep crosses into the box towards Fernandes and Cunha.

Against physical central defenders, that simply does not work. If Michael Carrick sticks with this system against City, United must alter their crossing strategy.



Rashford, Luke Shaw, or Patrick Dorgu need to work combinations to get in behind near the byline.

From there, they shouldn’t hit deep hanging crosses, but rather sharp cut-backs into the penalty area as arriving runners crash the box.

Playing against City is completely different.

City will dominate territory higher up the pitch, meaning United desperately need a “postman” – the man you play the ball up to as you look to attack.

Whether Carrick selects Benjamin Sesko or Cunha for that role, the “postman” is the focal point who receives the initial pass out from defence.



He acts as the post for the attackers to play off, allowing the rest of the team to push up and progress forward.

This becomes vital because Maresca has introduced a man-for-man high press.

We saw against Porto how City’s full-backs and midfielders jump forward to shadow their opponents.



When Matheus Nunes or a central midfielder jumps out of position to press, it leaves massive gaps right in front of City’s backline.

A disciplined postman standing between the lines will easily receive vertical passes from deep and trigger deadly counter-attacks.

CLONE RANGERS

Can Fernandez, Cherki, and Foden all play together in the same City midfield? Absolutely – and it could be sensational to watch.

In Maresca’s 3-1-6 structure, Nunes pushes high to give width on the right, Gvardiol tucks into the back three, and Anderson or Ayyoub Bouaddi sits as the single pivot.

That allows Foden, Cherki and Fernandez to operate in the half-spaces right on the edge of the opposition penalty box.



These three are like ‘Clone Rangers’ — technically gifted playmakers who thrive in tight areas.

They constantly interchange positions. If Foden drops deep to demand the ball, Cherki drifts into his space, and Fernandez surges into the box.

United will want to keep their defensive lines narrow, but the movement of these three inside tight gaps can dismantle any low block.

The crucial glue holding this together is Fernandez. Much like Bernardo Silva did for Guardiola, Fernandez acts as City’s tactical Swiss Army knife.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

While Foden and Cherki are pure attackers, Fernandez possesses the defensive awareness and work rate to cover ground rapidly.



When United attempt their quick bounce pass out of defence, Fernandez will be the man tasked with anticipating the play, stepping in to regain possession in the transition, and immediately setting City back on the attack.

Sports.title: Eight wonderkids Arsenal signed in summer transfer window as Mikel Arteta and Co add serious firepower to academy
Sports.content:
ARSENAL may have had a somewhat underwhelming transfer window for their first team, but they added some serious firepower to their academy.

The Gunners signed eight players to their Hale End ranks during the summer window, investing in future stars that could grow into senior talent.



Last season was something of a disappointment for Arsenal at academy level, as the Under-21s finished 14th out of 29 teams in the Premier League 2 and were eliminated in the group stages of the EFL Trophy.

But a summer of change has sparked an academy revamp that has been backed by a slew of new arrivals.



The U21s are now under the management of David Horseman, while academy director Pascal De Maesschalck has replaced Per Mertesacker at a more senior level.

Here SunSport Arsenal Reporter Joshua Hall breaks down all eight of the new signings to Arsenal’s academy ranks.



JAMES SCANLON

Age: 19

Position: Winger

Signed from: Manchester United

Scanlon is already an experienced professional, racking up 24 senior caps for his country, Gibraltar, and spending the second half of last season on loan from League Two side Swindon.

The winger, who describes himself as a “creative player”, was highly thought of at Man Utd, but has been convinced to make the jump to the Gunners.

Scanlon has already impressed, scoring on his U21s debut for Arsenal against Brighton earlier this week.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

IGOR TYJON

Age: 18

Position: Striker

Signed from: Blackburn Rovers



Arsenal had been chasing Tyjon for over a year and finally got their man this summer, having come close to signing the ace last January.

The highly-rated striker was subject to bids in excess of £1m during his time at Blackburn, having made his senior debut for the club aged just 16.

Tyjon is a sharp-shooter with an impressive goalscoring record and has represented both England and Poland at youth level.

ELIJAH UPSON

Age: 18

Position: Centre-back

Signed from: Tottenham Hotspur

The son of former Arsenal and England ace Matthew Upson, Elijah Upson has crossed the North London divide to join the Gunners from Tottenham.

Spurs had been hoping to keep hold of the young defender, but Upson decided to reject a pro contract and make the switch to Arsenal.



Upson is known for his power at the back and can be a threat in both boxes thanks to his physicality, but is also impressive with the ball at his feet when playing out from the back.

PHOENIX BLAYNEY

Age: 15

Position: Goalkeeper

Signed from: Larne

Blayney has penned pre-contract terms with Arsenal that will see him sign a pro deal when he turns 17.

The young goalkeeper actually spent a brief period on trial with Arsenal before joining from Northern Irish club Larne last month.



Blayney has already represented Northern Ireland U17s eight times, despite being just 15 years old.

AXEL DONCZEW

Age: 16

Position: Winger

Signed from: Cardiff City

A massive coup for Arsenal, Donczew became the youngest player to ever play for Cardiff City when he made his first team debut at just 15 years old.

Like Blayney, the Welshman will sign professional terms when he turns 17 after agreeing a pre-contract at Arsenal.

Donczew is an impressive dribbler with an eye for goal and has represented Wales at Under-19 level despite his young age.



HABEEB OGUNNEYE

Age: 20

Position: Right-back

Signed from: Manchester United

Man Utd have lost two top talents to Arsenal this summer, with Ogunneye joining Scanlon in moving to the capital.

Like Scanlon, Ogunneye has already got some senior football under his belt, having played 22 times for League Two Newport County on loan last season.

The powerful full-back never made his first-team debut but was chosen on the bench for a host of Premier League matches during Erik ten Hag’s stint at Old Trafford.

MYLO BERNARD

Age: 16

Position: Striker

Signed from: Crystal Palace

Bernard has penned a pre-contract with Arsenal, joining as a first-year scholar ahead of signing professional terms when he turns 17 next year.



The highly-rated striker scored more than 40 GOALS for Palace’s academy teams last season, catching the eye of clubs across the country.

His performances also earned him a call-up to Palace’s Under-18s team, where he netted six times in the U18 Premier League despite his young age.

ANDRIA BARTISHVILI

Age: 17

Position: Winger/Attacking midfield

Signed from: Kolkheti 1913

Dubbed “the next Kvaratshkelia”, Bartishvili has been tipped for a huge future in his home country of Georgia.

The teenager will join Arsenal officially in July, after he turns 18.

Bartishvili has incredibly quick feet and is always looking to make something happen when he is on the ball.



His talent has not gone unnoticed, with Liverpool and Juventus also scouting him over the past year, but it is Arsenal who have secured the youngster’s signature.

Sports.title: Man Utd confirm 685 season ticket bans as touting investigation sparks furious backlash
Sports.content:
Man Utd confirm 685 season ticket bans as touting investigation sparks furious backlash

Manchester United have announced the results of their controversial investigation into ticket touting at Old Trafford, which has sparked a planned protest this weekend

View 3 Images Manchester United fans have criticised the club's investigation (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

Manchester United have removed 685 season tickets following a lengthy and much-criticised investigation into touting at Old Trafford.

‌



Back in August, the club identified 1,617 accounts exhibiting "unusual activity". The holders of those accounts were then contacted and asked to provide explanations for the activity that was deemed suspicious.

‌



This heavy-handed approach sparked a furious backlash among supporters, with many believing that innocent and loyal fans were unfairly being accused. A protest ahead of Sunday's Manchester Derby at Old Trafford has been called over what fan group The 1958 said were sanctions being made without "compelling evidence".

‌



United have now announced the results of their investigation, which allowed fans to appeal to an independent appeals panel. The club said 685 season tickets were revoked, including 499 whereby a ban was upheld by the appeals panel.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Meanwhile, 468 cases were resolved after the season ticket holder provided information to exonerate themselves. The club have admitted they "did not anticipate the extent" to which fans shared account details "in circumstances they regarded as legitimate" and in those cases no sanctions were imposed.

The club said in a statement: "Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts.

"These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United.

‌



"Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list."

View 3 Images Manchester United fans are unhappy with the way the touting investigation was carried out (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

The club added: "We want to allow any sanctioned ticket holder the opportunity to refer their case to the Independent Football Ombudsman. Therefore, we will wait until after the international break before reallocating season tickets.

‌



"Any seats used on a match-by-match basis before then will be sold at season ticket prices, not matchday prices. The club is not profiting from this process."

The club said 226 accounts received final warnings for breaking rules but not for financial gain, while 238 accounts guilty of further abuses saw their initial season ticket ban reduced to a ban on home ticket forwarding and away match applications.

Speaking before the club's announcement on Friday, Chris Rumfitt, a spokesperson for Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST), summed up the ill feeling among fans.

‌



He told Mirror Football: "If it was a clampdown on touting we would be entirely supportive, because the biggest losers of touting are fans who get exploited and ripped off.

View 3 Images Ticket prices have been another bone of contention (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

"But what they are calling a clampdown on touting has brought up a huge numbers of match-going fans doing ordinary things match-going fans do, i.e. passing tickets between groups of friends at face value, which people wouldn't consider to be touting.

‌



"There is no question that large number of ordinary fans have been caught up in this because what the club has defined as 'suspicious' included lots of things fans do."

Rumfitt believes the issue has touched such a nerve with supporters that only the botched attempt to form a European Super League five years ago compares to the strength of feeling in the stands.

He added: "The approach the club has taken has been 'ban first, ask questions later'. They've banned people and then asked them to prove that they haven't done anything wrong, which isn't normally how things work in this country. The burden of proof works the other way around.

Article continues below

"There's a massive amount of discontent among all fan groups, it's really united the fans. The way the club has gone about this is completely wrong. It has spread further mistrust."

Sports.title: Gary Speed’s mum devastates viewers in heartbreaking Dan Walker interview - 'I feel ashamed’
Sports.content:
Gary Speed’s mum devastates viewers in heartbreaking Dan Walker interview - 'I feel ashamed’

It's been almost 15 years since Gary Speed's death sent shockwaves through football.

View 2 Images Gary Speed died in November 2011. (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

The mother of Gary Speed, Carol, has made the heartbreaking admission that she feels ‘ashamed’ almost 15 years on from his death. The former Wales manager was found dead in his home in November 2011, sending shockwaves through football.

‌



His death came just the day after he appeared on Football Focus alongside presenter Dan Walker. In an interview, Walker and Carol Speed shared an emotional moment as they talked about Speed. The chat was part of the suicide prevention toolkit On Your Side, which the Prince and Princess of Wales have helped to launch.

‌



"I was numb for a long time, when that numbness sort of cleared a bit I just wanted to go with him,” Carol Speed admitted to Walker on Channel 5 News.

‌



FIFA respond after Morocco claim they are hosting 2030 World Cup final READ MORE :

England U21s all-time top goalscorer asked to change allegiance despite senior cap READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"He's always on my mind. I just miss him, I miss him everyday really.

"I feel quite ashamed that I should have known that he was struggling but he didn't give us any idea to look at him. He had a big smile on his face and he seemed settled but obviously something was troubling him.

‌



"It's hard to come to terms with, even now after 15 years that, well, I should've been there for him."

Walker then said: "I spent that last day with him, we were on TV together and I think most weeks I will think about things I should've seen that day or things I could have asked him.

"Could I have rung him on his way home? What could I have seen? I was somebody who was a good friend of his but I only came across him every now and again. You were his mum so that does hurt, doesn't it?

‌



"People bring you their memories of Gary and you see the way he had that effect on people and yet he only had one mum and your that person who loved him as a kid and still loves him as much now."

Carol highlighted how, on the outside, her son had an ideal life, but that doesn’t tell the whole story. "He had a lovely family, successful career, not short of money,” she said. “And yet people on the outside looking in think what's he got to worry about, but it's just what's in your head isn't it."

Walker replied: "I think that's the thing Carol, he was successful, he did have an amazing family who loved him, he was doing well with Wales, he had a brilliant career, and everybody looked at that and thought how can somebody like Gary feel like that.”

‌



When asked how she gets up in the morning, given the death of her husband earlier this year, Carol said: "With great difficulty.

"I don't know. I just go from day to day but it's hard to get out of bed in the morning, even now, after 15 years. Gary never spoke to us about it, we didn't have an inkling, and it was something that never crossed my mind. It always happened to someone else sort of thing."

At the end of the interview, Walker ended by saying: “I don't end most interviews with a hug, but can we hug? Lovely to see you, look after yourself Carol.”

‌



View 2 Images Carol Speed talks to the Prince and Princess of Wales. (Image: Shirlaine Forrest/Getty Images)

As part of the launch at Everton ’s Hill Dickinson Stadium, Carol also spoke to the Prince and Princess of Wales about her son.

“Before Gary passed it was a stigma, it wasn't spoken about,” she said. “Since then it seems to have come out more. People are talking about it more and it needs to do even more so.

Article continues below

"If people are struggling, talk to somebody and get it out in the open. Don't keep it to yourself."

Chelsea are nearing a new dawn with Behdad Eghbali solely at the helm of the Premier League giants. Alongside Todd Boehly, the billionaire co-founder of Clearlake Capital were behind a consortium of investors to buy the west London side in 2022 for £4.25billion.

Four years on from the purchase, the Iranian-American billionaire is closing in on full control of the football club. Reports emerged last month that negotiations had begun for Boehly, Mark Walter and Hansjorg Wyss to sell their shared 38.5% of Chelsea to Clearlake and Bloomberg now reports that a deal is nearing completion following an acceleration in talks in recent weeks.

‌



The potential sale would increase Eghbali and his firm's share in the club from 61.5% to 99.9%. According to Forbes, Eghbali, 50, has a net worth of £2.8bn, but even that staggering figure pales in comparison to some of the richest owners in the English top-flight.

‌



Standing at the top of the monetary conversation in the Premier League top-flight are Newcastle United's owners, the Public Investment Fund. The sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia tips the scale at £1.2trillion, with Liverpool's ownership combination of Fenway Sports Group (FSG) and Jeff Bezos' backed consortium possessing a net worth of £265bn in second place.

The new investment group at Anfield is headed by former QPR owner Amit Bhatia, who is the son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mitta, whose net worth sits at around £22bn. The Amazon founder is the third-richest individual in the world and has a net worth of £198bn.

Sports.content:
Man Utd told to build side around Kobbie Mainoo despite £155m summer transfer spend

Kobbie Mainoo was linked with a move away from Manchester United this summer and was expected to fall down the pecking order after a window that saw the Red Devils add to their midfield options

View 2 Images Kobbie Mainoo has impressed for Manchester United this season (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has been told to make Kobbie Mainoo the central part of his Manchester United side. Mainoo, 21, has played a crucial role for the Red Devils this season.

‌



He has started three out of their opening four games of the campaign, turning in eye-catching performances against Everton and Sabah in the Champions League.

‌



His contribution is all the more remarkable given that United revamped their midfield in the summer - Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba all being signed for a combined £140m.

‌



Despite that, former United star Owen Hargreaves believes the youngster should be one of the first names on the team sheet. Speaking on TNT Sports, he said: "I’ve never seen Kobbie play bad. Every time I watch him play football, I think, 'How can somebody not play this young man?'

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"I just think he’s a fabulous football player. Academy-grown, didn’t cost a club a pound, and when you think about some of the fees that these players are going for. Obviously, they signed Santos and Tielemans for £85 million combined.

"Baleba was probably £70m. What would Kobbie be worth? It’s worth more than them all. No disrespect to any of them, but I just love his game."

He added: "You can just pass him the ball anywhere at any time. Technically, just so gifted, glides with the ball. That’s what a Man United midfielder needs to do at all times. Obviously, with Bruno in front of him, whether he plays as a six or an eight, he’s what you build around. He’s a star. I think he’s going to be a superstar. He’s only 21 years old, and he plays like he’s 30. That’s how he plays football in the most stressful environment – just chilled."

‌



View 2 Images Mainoo already has three starts for Man Unites this season (Image: Getty Images)

United boss Michael Carrick is also a massive fan. Speaking after his side's win against Sabah, he said: "He's a fantastic player, Kobbie. I think it's pretty obvious to see, you know, the way he is performing, playing that little bit deeper really and connecting the attacks.

"[He's] starting the attacks and having a massive influence on our games. So, he's a real joy to have. He wants to learn, he wants to improve, he wants to listen. And he expresses himself on the pitch, you know, and it's great to see."

Sports.title: FIFA respond after Morocco claim they are hosting 2030 World Cup final
Sports.content:
FIFA respond after Morocco claim they are hosting 2030 World Cup final

FIFA has been forced to respond after 2030 World Cup Final claims

View 2 Images FIFA have released a statement after claims around the 2030 World Cup final (Image: PA Wire)

FIFA has reiterated that a decision will be made in due course on where the 2030 World Cup final will be held, with the tournament taking place in Morocco and Spain. The statement comes after the Morocco Football Federation president made the claim that the final would be held at the Grand Stade Hassan II in Casablanca, even though the stadium is still under construction.

‌



Speaking at a political rally on Thursday, Moroccan federation president Fouzi Lakjaa told those in attendance that his nation had been successful in securing the final. He said: "The city of Benslimane will host the World Cup final. Hate it or love it, and if anyone wants to talk on top of that, let them talk.

‌



"The city is Benslimane, the Hassan II stadium is the stadium, and I hope that Morocco will be playing it."

‌



Lisandro Martinez trolls Jamie Carragher as Man Utd star leaves Micah Richards in hysterics READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes injury scare as Man Utd star seen 'limping' ahead of Manchester derby READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

FIFA have had to deny that a decision has been made, reiterating in a statement that an announcement would be made in 'due course.'

The latest debacle follows on from FIFA having to deny it had promised Morocco the final of the 2030 tournament - which is being held in the African nation, Spain and Portugal - in exchange for its support of Gianni Infantino at next month's FIFA elections.

‌



As well as those three countries, Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay will host the opening matches for their respective national teams during the tournament as a tribute to the 100 years since the 1930 World Cup, which was held in Montevideo.

View 2 Images The 2030 World Cup is being held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco (Image: PA)

Nevertheless, the head of the Spanish football federation, Rafael Louzan, insisted that Spain should be rewarded the honour of hosting the final.

‌



He said: "We all signed to accept the candidacy ... it's too bad that, regarding the final, it wasn't made clear, totally clear, where it is to be played. Spain, as world champion both in men's and women's football, must host the final."

The King Hassan II Stadium is being built in Benslimate on the outskirts of Casablanca and will have a capacity of 115,000 specators, while the Barcelona's Nou Camp and the Bernabeu are also possible destinations for the final.

The recently renovated Bernabeu holds 78,297, while the Nou Camp is also currently being renovated and its new capacity will be 105,000

Article continues below

FIFA chief Infantino has held two meetings with King Mohammed VI, with the most recent a crisis meeting back in August.

There's also ongoing political disputes between Spain and Morocco, with thousands of migrants crossed into Cueta, the Spanish enclave that borders Morocco with 140 people dying.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals bizarre traps including air con trick to stop Arsenal stars 'panicking'
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta reveals bizarre traps including air con trick to stop Arsenal stars 'panicking'

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed small pranks he has played on his squad in order to keep them on their toes and prevent them from 'panicking'

View Image Arteta has revealed some strange tricks he has played on his players (Image: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has been playing bizarre mind games to bolster Arsenal’s title defence.

‌



Arteta set quirky “challenges” for his players in pre-season to stop them “panicking” when things do go wrong in the Premier League campaign.

‌



Gunners boss Arteta deliberately turned up the heating in the dressing room, made them late for plane and coach journeys and disrupted meal times and removed massage beds.

‌



It probably paid off this week when Arsenal’s flight to Naples was delayed for three hours and Arteta says the pre-season tricks were good preparation for the season ahead.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Arteta said: “I love those challenges. I try to clear them in pre-season. So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know.

“So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there's so much traffic, and I don't want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking.

‌



“So, when that happens, adapt to it. Okay, we have another two or three hours on the plane, how can we use them? Play together, spend some time together, sleep, use it, but certainly don't complain and then use it as an excuse because that's not helpful at all.

“Just delaying the meals, delaying the transport, taking a different route. We've done many things, made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds.

Mikel Arteta fires back at Gabriel Jesus as row over bitter Arsenal transfer exit escalates READ MORE :

“Those kind of things, I think, in my opinion, because we're going to have to adapt to different contexts, and we'll try to anticipate it and create the best possible conditions. But when there is not that element of surprise or stress on match day, I think it's important.”

‌



It is not the first time Arteta has done whacky things to keep the players on their toes.

In the past, Arteta even got a team of pick pockets to prey on the players during a dinner to keep them on their toes.

Arteta also used messaging last season and used the word “fire” to gee up his players having set up a bonfire at the training ground and telling them to write down their fears and throw the paper into the blaze.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher warns Michael Carrick he faces same problem as Gareth Southgate
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher warns Michael Carrick he faces same problem as Gareth Southgate

Manchester United have won just one of their three Premier League games so far this season - after a brilliant start to life in the dugout for Michael Carrick

View 2 Images Manchester United manager Michael Carrick during the win over Sabah

Jamie Carragher believes Michael Carrick will always be just a few bad results away from his Manchester United future being in question.

‌



Carrick was appointed as caretaker back in January, following the sacking of Ruben Amorim. And the former midfielder had an immediate impact taking United from seventh place into the top three and back into the Champions League.

‌



Despite only being hired as an interim, Old Trafford bosses postponed their search for a new manager, instead giving the reins to Carrick permanently.

‌



However, his first full season in charge has got off to an underwhelming start with United winning just one of their first three games in the league. That also included an opening-day defeat to Hull City, which immediately led to questions about Carrick’s suitability for the job.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



And Liverpool legend Carragher believes that’s an issue that will continue to haunt Carrick, with some believing he is still a glorified caretaker, waiting for a bigger name to replace him.

He told the Telegraph: "My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

“To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.”

‌



View 2 Images Carrick has helped transform Man Utd's fortunes since replacing Ruben Amorim (Image: Getty Images)

In 20 Premier League matches in the dugout, Carrick has an impressive 13 wins and just three defeats, picking up 43 points from a possible 60. But Carragher says that like ex-England boss Gareth Southgate, his CV will always be used against him.

He added: “To be blunt, Carrick faces an issue which haunted Gareth Southgate during his stint as England manager. He is a bad result or coaching decision away from that thorny question: does someone who was sacked by Middlesbrough truly deserve one of the biggest jobs in football?”

‌



Carrick’s United face Manchester City on Sunday, as he looks to repeat one of the statement results in his tenure so far. And they go into that on the back of a dominant win in their Champions League opener.

United were 3-0 to the good against minnows Sabah, allowing the manager to take off Youri Tielemans at the break and Kobbie Mainoo at the hour mark. He also rested Luke Shaw in a bid to make sure he is fit and firing for the first derby of the season.

Sports.title: Antonelli sets pace as Lindblad suffers first F1 crash at challenging Madring
Sports.content:
World championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest on Formula 1's first day of running at the Spanish Grand Prix's new Madrid circuit as the hugely challenging nature of the Madring was exhibited by a big crash for British rookie Arvid Lindblad.

After being outpaced by his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the day's first session, Antonelli produced a quicker time of 1:33.662 in Practice Two to edge out Ferrari duo Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton by little more than a tenth of a second.

The timesheet was further evidence of Antonelli's sky-high confidence, which was elevated by a stunning victory at the Italian Grand Prix last weekend as he won his home race from 19th on the grid to move 66 points clear of Russell at the top of the standings with 10 rounds of the 2026 season remaining.

On the evidence of Friday's sessions, Mercedes and Ferrari are closely matched and could deliver an exciting pole contest in qualifying on Saturday, with huge excitement in the Spanish capital as F1 returns to the city for the first time since 1981.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arvid Lindblad brought out the first red flag at the Madring track after this heavy crash on turn 13 during second practice

Many had predicted a high number of red flags on Friday - and throughout the rest of the weekend - due to the tight and punishing nature of a circuit that the field have never raced at before.

While there were several crashes and red flags in Friday's F2 and F3 sessions, the F1 drivers showed their excellence to avoid any major incidents in first practice, but it was Lindblad who came unstuck just beyond the halfway point of Practice Two.

The 19-year-old was driving impressively and had just elevated himself to fourth when he pushed too hard on his next flying lap, losing control at Turn 13 and spinning into the barrier at high speed.

Lindblad said: "It's not an easy track. We are all pushing to find the limits. It's new for all of us. Just made a bit of a mistake and overdid it in Turn 13. A shame. I apologise to the mechanics and the team. It's extra work for them tonight.

"But looking at the big picture, it's been a good day. We are very fast. I was running P4 on merit and was only two tenths from P1 which is really strong.

"A lot of confidence in the team going into tomorrow. I'm just focused on resetting and trying to block it out and taking all the good learnings."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player F2's Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak walks away after his car went up in flames!

A delay of just over 10 minutes put an end to the qualifying simulations that had been taking place at that stage, securing Antonelli's position at the top of the timesheet.

Russell was fifth after appearing to struggle to optimise his setup, but still managed to edge out Red Bull's Max Verstappen and McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

"It was fun to drive the track for the first time," Russell said. "It's always a great experience driving a new circuit.

"FP1 was a strong session. FP2 we made some setup changes which weren't quite as good, so we will probably revert back on that. So far so good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Several drivers were left frustrated by Lewis Hamilton for getting in the way during first practice of the Spanish Grand Prix

Reigning world champion Lando Norris was unable to set a time after a gearbox failure took him out of the session after just two laps.

McLaren were expected to be competitive in Madrid given Norris had claimed back-to-back victories before Antonelli's win in Monza, but there was little evidence of that on Friday.

While Norris has generally been quicker than Piastri recently, losing an entire session at a new circuit will put the Brit on the back foot going into Saturday.

Sports.title: Stokes back in top flight of County Championship as Durham secure promotion
Sports.content:
Durham clinched promotion to Division One of the Rothesay County Championship with a 93-run victory over Middlesex at Chester-le-Street.

The north-east side began the final day needing eight wickets and Kasey Aldridge struck with the first ball to set the tone.

Despite a battling unbeaten ton from Harry Duke alongside Ben Geddes' half-century, Durham took control with the ball as Callum Parkinson finished with four wickets for 45 runs and Brydon Carse also claimed four to secure their spot back in the top flight next year.

Elsewhere in Division Two, Gloucestershire secured a 105-run win over Lancashire, with JT Langridge putting in an impressive performance with the ball.

The bowler struck early to remove both George Balderson and Noman Ali before Sai Kishore claimed Mitchell Stanley's wicket.

Langridge secured victory for Gloucestershire and completed a five-wicket haul by dismissing Rocky Flintoff for 65.

Hampshire remain under pressure in Division One following a 54-run defeat to Nottinghamshire.

Sports.title: Kings of Manchester: Who will reign when United and City clash?
Sports.content:
Manchester City have been "the Kings of Manchester".

That coronation came from City's £116m summer signing Elliot Anderson - and has been hotly debated in the build-up to the Manchester derby Super Sunday showdown at Old Trafford, which you can watch live on Sky Sports.

Is Anderson right? Does City's huge recent success mean they rule the roost? Or are Manchester United still No 1?

What did Anderson say?

Anderson was asked about the Manchester derby during an interview with Manchester City's official club website this summer.

"It's one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester," Anderson said.

"It'll be a great fixture and I can't wait to be involved in something like that."

Maresca 'excited' by 'special' Manchester derby

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca explains that Elliot Anderson's pre-season 'kings of Manchester' comment was most likely born out of the fact that the midfielder grew up in a period of Manchester City domination

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says Anderson's verdict rings true in recent years.

"Probably the reason why Elliot said that was that he grew up in the last 15 years, Manchester City were unbelievable with what they achieved. It's normal Elliot said that," said Maresca.

"If you go back, then it's a different picture but when he grew up Manchester City were dominant."

Speaking in an interview with Sky Sports, Maresca outlined the importance of these Manchester match-ups to all involved.

"It's special because it's two teams in the same city. It's special for the fans, the club, for everyone," said Maresca.

"I'm very excited. These are the games I like. These are the games we want. We know it's going to be a tough game. Since Michael [Carrick] took over they're doing a fantastic job. We can show respect in the derby by trying to be ourself and go there to try to win."

Carrick on how the derby changed

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick refused to be drawn into Elliot Anderson's claim that Manchester City are the 'Kings of Manchester' ahead of Sunday's derby

Michael Carrick was a Manchester United player when City were labelled "noisy neighbours" by former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson in 2009. But the current United head coach says City's subsequent Premier League wins and triumphs in the derby have ramped up the rivalry.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Carrick said: "When I first came to the club, to be honest, it wasn't like it is now.

"In 20 years, it's kind of grown, it's developed, it's changed a little bit over the years."

Carrick pinpoints Vincent Kompany's derby winner in April 2012 - a month before City's last-day Premier League title triumph - as a key moment in the duel for supremacy in Manchester.

Image: Vincent Kompany heads in a Manchester derby winner in April 2012

"The one where we ended up losing the league, when Kompany scored the header towards the end of the season. We had a bit of a lead and then we lost it, and then we lost it at the end of the season. That felt quite a big moment," he said.

"That's just the one that we lost, so it probably hurts. We always remember those ones the most."

There have been glorious derby days for United, too, which Carrick remembers more fondly.

"Probably the [2010 League Cup] semi-final is up there, when we won late and I scored and Wayne [Rooney] scored a header. That was a good day.

Manchester United

"Robin [Van Persie] scoring in the last minute [in the Premier League win at the Etihad in December 2012] the last time we won the league.

"When Michael [Owen] scored that one at the Stratford End [in September 2009]."

"Wayne's overhead kick in 2011? I forgot about that one! That was a special one."

Carrick is now hoping to add to that list. "There were some really good games over the years, hopefully we can come out on top on Sunday."

Sky Sports' Paul Merson:

Manchester United have got the Manchester derby - and their season is in the balance too. If you beat Manchester City, you're flying. If you get beat by Manchester City, here we go again.

It would be one point from two games including the Everton game. And other teams are winning around you.

So I am worried - and this is why I didn't put Manchester United in my top five at the start of the season. Nothing's changed for me since then. When you draw games, it hurts you.

shree: City have won a lot recently and you know it's all because of oil money and a world class coach. United haven't been best in recent years but the point we are still doing this comparison itself shows how great a club Manchester United are which City won't be able to be.

Argyle loyal: At this moment in time it's definitely City, the days of United being kings of Manchester went when Fergie left.

Aaron s: I think it has to be Man U. Look at their history. Man U just played and won their 300th Champions League game. Look at the amount of trophies they have won compared to Manchester City. City may have become bigger recently but Man U are and will always be the kings of Manchester.

PeteUK: Remember when United fans jumped on Liverpool fans for 'living in the past'? How the tables have dramatically turned, United are Kings like Arthur: relegated to history books.

Woop: I think City are the better side and have been over the last 15 years but Manchester United are a bigger football club. I don't see United winning a league for a long time though whereas city will.

Shanepancho778: As a lifelong Liverpool fan it's nice to finally say that Manchester is definitely blue and will be for the foreseeable future. Those glory days left in 2013 when Ferguson retired.

Sports.title: Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Doncaster Cup
Sports.content:
Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointing efforts at Royal Ascot and York to win the Betfred Howards Wright Doncaster Cup.

Questions had been raised over whether the five-year-old still had the stomach for the fight after coming home last in the Gold Cup and stopping quickly before finishing fourth in the Lonsdale Cup at York.

But after taking up the running a furlong from home on Town Moor under Oisín Murphy, the George Scott-trained stayer proved his doubters wrong, pulling away from Beylerbeyi to land odds of 5-6 favourite by a length and a quarter.

The race had been robbed of its likely favourite after Queenstown was pulled out and there was also drama beforehand when the Emmet Mullins-trained Winday gave trouble at the start. Having worked himself up into a sweat, he failed to the fire in the race itself, finishing a tailed off last of seven.

Scott is now looking forward to seeing his charge defend his title in the Prix du Cadran on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp.

He said: "We needed to see that from him today if we wanted to go back to Paris with him, as he's two from two there - we just have to hope Scandinavia doesn't turn up there. If he doesn't then he's going to be a player.

"He loves Longchamp, he loves the tempo of the races and two-mile-four is right up his street.

"I thought he was value for a bit more today, he had to commit earlier than he wanted."

The Doncaster Cup was been robbed of its likely favourite after Queenstown was pulled out and there was also drama beforehand when the Emmet Mullins-trained Winday gave trouble at the start. Having worked himself up into a sweat, he failed to the fire in the race itself, finishing a tailed off last of seven.

But on this occasion Caballo De Mar was as good as gold, much to the delight of his trainer.

"His last two races have been in a Gold Cup against two of the best stayers we've seen, and he was third until the furlong pole, and last time at York they went a hell of a gallop and he was in the thick of it the whole way. York is a funny track too, they can misfire and he did," Scott continued.

"Today was a much more of an even set up for him, so I think it's more down to circumstance than anything.

"This horse has been amazing for us for two years - he's had two bad runs, so what - some horses go off the boil for a year before coming back but we got him back within three weeks.

"I said to Sheikh Nasser (owner) this morning, he's a world class athlete and you can train in the gym all you like but if you come out in the afternoon in the heat of battle, that is when you see true colours.

"In the paddock I knew he was on it and Oisin said straight away 'he's here'.

"Victorious Racing put an awful lot of trust in me so it is a relief he's won today. I know that if it goes wrong they have got my back."

Final Objective gets up to land thrilling Flying Childers

Gimcrack runner-up Final Objective came out on top in a thrilling climax to the Carlsberg Danish Pilsner Flying Childers Stakes.

Hamad Al Jehani's juvenile has steadily improved with racing this season, most recently going down by three-quarters of a length to Arapaho Gold at York last month.

Dropping back to five furlongs for the first time, the gelded son of Sioux Nation was a 9-4 favourite in the hands of James Doyle, who produced his mount with a perfectly-timed challenge to get up in the shadows of the post.

Image: Final Objective (blue) triumphed in the Flying Childers

Crownbreaker finished a neck second, with Flann Sunna and long-time leader Fast Track close up in third and fourth. In The Black was unfortunate not to do better than fifth after encountering trouble in running before clipping heels and almost coming down passing the line.

Doyle said: "He's a testament to Hamad and his team because he has not been an easy conveyance whatsoever.

"Faleh [Bughenaim], our Qatari jockey, has done a brilliant job with him because he rides him every day so he has to suffer on a daily basis while I only ride him now and again so I have to thank him.

"He was a bit wayward again late on but that is just his nature, he's a bit tricky.

"I was just trying to hang on to their coattails because I was a little bit outpaced early. He's got decent form at six and this was his first time back at five. It wasn't a problem as he's got more than enough speed.

"I thought he was going to win the Gimcrack but when he got out he hung his chance away and I thought he was going to do a similar thing today. He's not easy but he's more straightforward than he used to be."

Forbidden Fire holds off Rock Montreal to win Flying Scotsman

Forbidden Fire resisted the late surge of Rock Montreal to claim top honours in the Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes.

Nine runners went to post for the Listed opener on day two of Doncaster's St Leger Festival and the market was dominated by two Godolphin-owned colts, with Charlie Appleby's dual winner Nabati the even-money favourite ahead of Roger Varian's impressive Yarmouth scorer Rock Montreal at 5-2.

Forbidden Fire, one of only two fillies in the field, was third best in the market at 9-2 off the back of a dominant debut victory at Salisbury, but showed the boys the way home under Murphy.

A daughter of No Nay Never out of owner-breeder Jeff Smith's top-class racemare Arabian Queen, Andrew Balding's filly travelled strongly and had most of her rivals in trouble a furlong out, with Rock Montreal one of the first under pressure at the rear of the field.

However, the latter began to find his stride against the near side rail late on and only missed out on victory by a head, with Nabati beaten into third.

Sports.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Backing Pierre Bonnard to bag 10th Leger for O'Brien
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle marks your card for the 250th St Leger and a stellar undercard at Doncaster on Saturday - live on Sky Sports Racing – and has a look at Leopardstown.

Pierre crying out for Leger trip

Who stands in the way of Aidan O'Brien and a brilliant 10th success in the world's oldest Classic, the Betfred St Leger Stakes (3.35) at Doncaster on Saturday? He saddles four runners on the 250th anniversary of the great race including probable favourite Christmas Day, who is bidding to become the first Derby winner to triumph since Reference Point 39 years ago.

Aidan's son Joseph O'Brien looks the most likely opponent to spoil the Ballydoyle party with the impressive Enceladus, who steps up to Group One company for the first time after excelling in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Group Three Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

However, I believe Aidan can complete the feat - not with Christmas Day but with his tough stable companion PIERRE BONNARD, who finished in front of him in the Great Voltigeur Stakes at York last month. This more demanding test of stamina is what he's been crying out for, and he can write his own piece of history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports Racing's Dave Orton has picked out his 1-2-3 prediction for Saturday's Leger at Doncaster, the 250th running of the race

Hurricane can storm home in Champagne

GENTLE HURRICANE left his novice win well behind when chasing home Haffner in the Group Three Acomb Stakes at York last month and can go one better in the Betfred Champagne Stakes (1.45) on Saturday. Andrew Balding's colt will be very much in his comfort zone over seven furlongs at Doncaster in this Group Two and can put that experience to good use in an open renewal.

Likely favourite Desert Castle made a big impression on debut at the July Course in Newmarket when he shot to the head of the 2,000 Guineas betting, but this represents a big step up in grade which poses questions.

Meanwhile, Willie Muir and Chris Grassick pitch Breacher into this higher grade following his promising third in the Group Three Solario Stakes at Sandown - a run that entitles him to be in the mix.

Return to seven the key to Thunder

Image: More Thunder and Tom Marquand heads to Doncaster on Saturday

It just hasn't been MORE THUNDER's year in top mile races but the return to seven furlongs in the Group Two Betfred Park Stakes (2.55) on Saturday can see him return to the winners' enclosure. He couldn't quite see out the trip after coming to win his race in the Prix Jacques le Marois last month but a strongly-run seven should play to his strengths.

Qirat, who ran a huge race to be second in the Celebration Mile at Goodwood, should ensure a searching, end-to-end gallop, along with Witness Stand, but my husband Tom Marquand's mount has the talent to overhaul them.

At a bigger price, I'd like to see Kevin Ryan's Volterra run a big race on his first start since being gelded. It's interesting that he's pitched straight into a race of this calibre after finishing second to Docklands at this track back in March.

Rumble the class act in Portland

The Betfred Portland Handicap (2.20) on Saturday is a tough puzzle to solve but the dash could go to Jack Channon's GETREADYTORUMBLE.

The four-year-old has run well in the face of some tough assignments in Listed and Group company this year and enjoyed the return top handicaps when beating all but one in a five-furlong sprint at Ascot in July. He must defy a career-high rating to win this cavalry charge, but I like the class angle.

I marginally prefer him to last year's winner Eternal Sunshine, who looks sure to make another bold bid under 5lbs claimer Laura Young. The duo tuned up with a good win at Hamilton last time while one of my favourites Toca Madera deserves to win a big handicap after a string of near misses at Goodwood and York this year.

River ready to avenge York defeat

Image: Constitution River wins the Qatar Prix du Jockey Club

What a race the Royal Bahrain Irish Champion Stakes (5.00) at Leopardstown on Saturday promises to be with the first three home in last month's Juddmonte International locking horns once again.

Item, who overhauled Almaqam in that Titanic duel, needs to prove he's as potent on this stiffer track as he is at York while Aidan O'Brien's CONSTITUTION RIVER sets out to prove his doubters wrong after that underwhelming run on The Knavesmire.

I'm prepared to forgive the brilliant French Derby and Eclipse winner that defeat as he simply pulled away his chance in the early part of the race. If Ryan Moore can get him to settle better, he can show what a great colt he is.

Almaqam deserves so much credit for getting within a whisker of winning the International and can show that was no fluke on a track and ground that will suit him. The quicker they go the better for Kieran Shoemark's likeable colt.

Bolt to complete Group 1 hat-trick

I can see no reason Andrew Balding can't continue his golden summer with the brilliant BLUE BOLT in the Coolmore America 'Justify' Matron Stakes (3.55) at Leopardstown on Saturday.

Unbeaten in all four starts this year, she can claim her third success at the highest level by confirming her superiority over Aidan O'Brien's Precise, who has finished behind her in both the Falmouth Stakes and the Prix Rothschild.

Aidan could control the race with both Precise and True Love being so well drawn but I still expect Blue Bolt to come out on top, while last year's winner Fallen Angel beat Juddmonte's star filly in last season's Sun Chariot and shouldn't be written off on ground she will enjoy.

Sports.title: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: ‘I’ve seen all of the meltdowns and it annoyed me’
Sports.content:
Transfer deadline day may be “exciting for everyone”, as Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall puts it, but his experience of that transfer deadline day at Everton hauled him through the same gamut of emotions as every Evertonian. Excitement turned to bewilderment before the conclusion of the window left the midfielder exasperated, but for entirely different reasons to a fanbase left questioning the club’s direction under The Friedkin Group.

How, now, is the mood in the squad? It is the obvious place to start after a deadline day that left David Moyes with fewer players than he had at the beginning, one striker and no cover for either full-back position. It also featured the US international striker Folarin Balogun walking out on a £40m transfer minutes after submitting a deal sheet. “Really good to be honest,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “Definitely not the same mood as what I’ve seen on the outside. There’s a good mentality this year of: ‘We’ll show everyone.’” Everton’s performances so far this season support that view.

“I’ve seen all of the reactions, all of the meltdowns, and in all honestly it annoyed me a bit,” Dewsbury-Hall says in forthright and insightful fashion. “I get where people are coming from; everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad. But there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded.

“I saw people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’ What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go – and that’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room. Of course we would have wanted to sign a couple more, but we’re happy with what we’ve got and it’s given us more impetus now to move on.”

Moyes has expressed concern over the signals Everton’s transfer business could send to the dressing room at a time when he is trying to push the team on. So has it had a detrimental impact? “Not really, no,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “I know we’ve got a smaller squad but we’ve got some really good players. Our starting XI is top, a European starting XI.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall says he needed his move to Everton to avoid his career stagnating. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“I get it, you need a whole squad, but we’ve got 17, 18 players at a really, really good level. I don’t think a couple of years ago it was at that level. Actually I know it wasn’t. Things can be out of your hands in football and that’s what happened for us. But we quickly realised: ‘Hang on a minute, look around the dressing room – top player, top player, top player.’ If we’re doing the right things we can still be successful.”

Dewsbury-Hall will be crucial to those prospects. The midfielder has flourished since his £28m arrival from Chelsea last summer, his game-time and growing influence vindicating the decision to leave Stamford Bridge behind. “I’m in the prime years of my career,” he says. “I couldn’t afford to spend more years stagnating.” The 28-year-old’s influence extends behind the scenes. This summer, following Séamus Coleman’s departure, he was nominated for a new leadership group that was established to compensate for the loss of the long-serving Everton captain.

“Because Séamus has left such a big hole we need a group of experienced lads to crack on together and keep the standards high and to drive things,” Dewsbury-Hall explains. “It’s just the more experienced lads – [Jordan] Pickford, Tarky [James Tarkowski, the new club captain], Jimmy [James] Garner, myself. The ones that have been playing in the Premier League for years or feel like they are settled at the club.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury Hall lets fly in Everton’s impressive 2-2 draw with Manchester United. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“It’s nice [to be voted in after just one season] but it’s definitely an impact I wanted to have. I’m really pleased that the lads look at me as someone that can be important for the dressing room.”

That sense of responsibility is evident in Dewsbury-Hall’s mentoring of fellow midfielder Harrison Armstrong, the 19-year-old who almost joined Nottingham Forest before deadline day only for the furious response of Evertonians at Bournemouth to prompt a U-turn from the club’s owners. “They definitely made their feelings known and obviously it worked,” says Dewsbury-Hall. “Big credit to them for that, they were amazing that day. And I know for a fact it made Harrison feel very good and it helped him. He is a very confident lad and well respected in the dressing room for such a young age.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“If there is anything I can help him with then I will. Shooting’s definitely one because his shooting is sometimes not the best, and I’ve told him that many times. But he’s got pretty much everything else. He always likes to say he’s got a better strike than me so I just tell him to look at the [Crystal] Palace goal [that Dewsbury-Hall scored on the opening day] or the Wolves goal last season. We have good banter.”

The Nottingham-born midfielder is clear in his targets for this season: European qualification, which he contends can be achieved despite the smaller squad, a strong cup run, improvement in his all-round game and a first England call-up. His rising performance levels have not gone unnoticed by Thomas Tuchel, who names his squad next Friday.

Dewsbury-Hall says: “I know I’m the closest I have ever been now. You get a message two weeks before the squad is announced. I got one for the long list for the World Cup and I’ve had one for these next games. It’s nice. It means you are doing OK. It’s a long, long message. It tells you that it’s a legal requirement for us [the Football Association] to tell you in advance that you are in contention and to be available for these dates. It’s a good feeling because you think: ‘OK, I am close,’ but you know you have to keep pushing it to the last minute. It’s up to me. It’s got to be me that forces his hand to choose me. It’s not going to be given to me.”

Nor will anything be given to Everton, but Dewsbury-Hall and company will push on regardless.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Mikel Arteta hits upon a new psychological wheeze for his champions
Sports.content:
THE MICROMANAGER FINAL BOSS

The use of psychological stratagems and pitchside or locker-room sabotage has long been employed by football managers trying to give their teams an edge over visiting rivals. Whether it’s placing the pegs too high or the seats too low, painting the walls an aggression-lowering shade of pink or deliberately moving the advertising hoardings to prevent long throws, there are apparently no stones conniving coaching staff will leave unturned if they think their team’s chances of winning may be improved by such shenanigans. Almost 40 years ago, Wimbledon’s Crazy Gang famously used to leave visitors to Plough Lane without any hot water, a plan that seemed stunning in its simplicity, until you realise – as Football Daily has just done after nearly 40 years – that footballers generally tend not to shower until after the game is over, rendering their attempt at disruption decidedly redundant.

A man who has previously attracted ridicule for hiring a team of pickpockets to pinch his players’ watches, phones and wallets during a team dinner to teach them the value of vigilance and focus, it ought to come as no surprise that Mikel Arteta has now hit upon the psychological wheeze of disrupting his own team’s preparations for matches as a way of keeping them on their toes. The Arsenal manager has revealed that he occasionally has dressing-room thermostats turned up to 11, delays meal and transport times, or has physio room massage beds “disappeared” to ensure Arsenal’s finest are prepared for any curveballs life might pitch their way. And while such half-baked amateur psychology will almost certainly provide more grist to the mill of Arteta haterz, if inducing mild anxiety in Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka over a toasty canteen or slightly late bus is all it takes to finally win a league title, then who are we to carp?

“I love those challenges,” parped Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-season. So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else. Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic, and I don’t want the players, the staff as well, panicking.” Of course, our more astute reader will have already clocked that Arsenal’s flight to Naples this week was delayed by several hours, prompting the cancellation of their pre-match press duties.

While Arsenal’s was only one of several hundred flights from UK airports disrupted or cancelled due to an air traffic control “glitch”, it behoves Football Daily to point out there is no suggestion that a slightly weird 44-year-old from San Sebastián was responsible for you and your pals missing out on that eagerly anticipated lads’ trip to Benidorm. We also know that while stressed-out passengers in overcrowded departure lounges across the UK were effing, jeffing and generally losing their minds, the footballers of Arsenal were – due in no small part to Arteta’s mind games – presumably waiting in the business lounge to board their well-appointed jet in a state of carefully orchestrated zen.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I quit and I’m not coming back” – Fenerbahce head coach Ismail Kartal announces his resignation after ⁠their 1-1 draw at home to Roma in Bigger Cup.

“Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it. I just spoke to [him]. He mentioned the bottle incident and he also complained about being under pressure … I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s ​it. We are a family” – Fenerbahce president Aziz Yildrim suggests Kartal will be coming back after all.

View image in fullscreen Ismail Kartal has a full and frank chat with assistant ref Diego Barbero. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

double quotation mark Thankfully Noble Francis has now won a book (yesterday’s Football Daily letters) so has something else to do other than writing prize-winning, witty missives. This means the rest of us mere mortals have a chance of winning your letter o’ the day” – Martyn Shapter.

If you have any, send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s letter o’ the day winner is … a rollover, so our final copy of The Mbappé Project by Philippe Auclair will be up for grabs on Monday. Copies are available in the Guardian Bookshop for you unlucky scribes. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.
